Design a detailed implementation plan for a "Nether-like dimension" epic in the voxel game at /Users/hutusi/workspace/ai/david/monecraft (Next.js 16 + React 19 + Three.js + TypeScript strict + Bun; single-player browser game with optional multiplayer via a Bun ws server; zero binary assets — all textures/sprites/sounds procedural).

## User decisions (fixed, do not revisit)
- ONE epic branch `feat/nether` off main, focused conventional commits per stage, one PR at the end. Lint green at each commit (bisectable).
- Three stages in order: (1) buckets & fluids precursor, (2) multi-dimension core + portal, (3) Nether content (standard scope).
- Dimension switch = SWAP-ON-TRAVEL: one live dimension at a time; portal travel autosaves the current dimension and rebuilds engine+renderer into the target via the existing shell remount path. No dual-live-worlds refactor.
- Single-player first: portal ignition in online worlds is refused with a toast; protocol stays v3; server must round-trip new save fields untouched.
- Standard content scope: netherrack, glowstone (+dust/lamp), lava-sea/cavern worldgen, a post-diamond ore tier (netherite-style), 2 new mobs (melee brute + ranged fire-shooter), nether advancements.

## Verified codebase facts (from exploration; trust these, spot-check as needed)

### Engine core
- `GameState` at lib/game/engine/state.ts:283-395 holds ONE `world: VoxelWorld` (state.ts:284) + `blockChanges` tracker (285). Containers Map keyed by voxel index (333), primedTnt (335), redstone cells (394), worldgen site sets dungeonChestIndices/shipwreckChestIndices/treasureSites/lootedWorldgenChests/villageSites (338-351) — all single flat voxel-index namespace. Mobs (358), vehicles (367-369), dayClock/daylight/weather (370-377). `worldMeshDirty` (383).
- `VoxelWorld` lib/world/voxelWorld.ts: 512×150×512 (blocks.ts:1-3), `blocks: Uint8Array`, `light: Uint8Array` derived cache, seed on the world (33). index = x + z*sizeX + y*sizeX*sizeZ.
- `generateWorld(world, worldType)` lib/world/generation.ts:149-194; `terrainConfigFor` (91-135) varies only seaLevel + per-biome heights; pass order generateTerrain→carveCaves→placeWater→placeBeaches→placeOres→placeCoal→placeLava→placeTrees→placeCacti→placeStructures→placeDungeons→placeVillages→placeShipwrecks→placeOceanFlora→placeBuriedTreasure. PRNG: mulberry32 seeded (seed>>>0)+0x6d2b79f5; decoupled per-pass streams xor seed with distinct constants (0x85ebca6b coal AND village — collision, avoid; 0x9e3779b9 dungeon; 0xc2b2ae35 shipwreck; 0x27d4eb2f treasure). The epic should wire this guard (nether worldgen changes will need it).
- GameEngine boot (GameEngine.ts:262-456): resolve seed → resolve worldType (save wins) → new VoxelWorld + generateWorld → collect*Sites → blockChanges.applySavedChanges(save.changes) → computeFullLight → spawn player → restore mobs/vehicles/containers/dayClock → forceUnstuck → spawnInitialMobs → seed villagers. serialize() at GameEngine.ts:1188-1205 writes version:17, seed, worldType, changes, blockEntities, lootedChests, mobs, vehicles, dayClock, players[].

Joiners get welcome{seed,worldType} + gzipped worldSync (changes/blockEntities/lootedChests/mobs/liveMobs/vehicles/projectiles/players) — buildWorldSync room.ts:520-535. - BlockId const enum lib/world/blocks.ts:5; highest = 89 (CobbleStairsWest); NEXT FREE = 90. Append-only (saved ids must never shift). Craft-only blocks need no WORLDGEN_VERSION bump; new worldgen writes to the OVERWORLD would. Redstone/rails use id-parity (even=off) — only relevant if a new block has power states.

Engine/UI stations (enchanting/anvil/grindstone) live on GameState.craftingStation not Recipe.station.

## Design questions the plan must answer (my leanings in parentheses — validate or improve)

### Stage 1 — buckets & fluids
1. Bucket item(s): craft from sliver/iron? empty_bucket / water_bucket / lava_bucket as kind:"material" non-stackable? Pickup: use empty bucket on Water/Lava block → filled bucket + block→Air. Place: use filled bucket → set block. Where in tryUseHeldItem vs placeBlock precedence?
2. NO flow simulation (static fluids) — confirm this is coherent (picking up ocean water leaves an air hole in water — acceptable? or refuse picking up "sea" water? MC-like infinite source? Simplest: picking up water just works, hole remains; document it).
3. Obsidian creation: water bucket used ON a Lava block converts it to Obsidian (MC-authentic-ish, gives purpose to deep lava). Obsidian mineable only with diamond pickaxe (mineTier 7), BREAK_HARDNESS very high. Also placeable/craftable? (just mined+replaceable).
4. Does lava become placeable → griefing/self-harm okay in SP; in MP the server engine validates anyway. Lava bucket useful as fuel? (skip — fuel is recipe-ingredient based).
5. WORLDGEN unchanged in stage 1 (no bump). Save unchanged? (buckets are just items — v17 untouched.) New blocks: Obsidian (id 90). Confirm.

### Stage 2 — multi-dimension core + portal
6. Dimension model: `type DimensionId = "overworld" | "nether"`. Where does it live? Proposal: SaveData gains `dimensions?: Partial<Record<DimensionId, DimensionSection>>` where DimensionSection = {changes, blockEntities?, lootedChests?, mobs?, vehicles?} — i.e., the world-half fields move/duplicate per dimension; top-level fields stay as the OVERWORLD's for backcompat (or migrate them into dimensions.overworld and keep writing both?). SavedPlayer gains `dimension?: DimensionId`. Save v17→v18 with migration. Design this carefully — the server room engine (overworld-only) must round-trip the nether section untouched through serialize() (pass-through field on the engine).
7. Engine boot: GameEngineOptions gains dimension; constructor picks the dimension's generator (generateWorld vs generateNetherWorld) + the dimension's save section. Sites collection per dimension (nether has its own or none initially). spawnInitialMobs / spawn directors become dimension-aware.
8. Portal travel flow (swap-on-travel): player stands in portal block N seconds (config) → engine emits `dimensionTravel` event with target + entry position → shell (useMinecraftGame) force-saves with player.dimension updated + position mapped → bumps reloadNonce → WorldSaveGate remounts → engine boots into target dimension → arrival portal ensured (search nearby for existing portal frame, else construct one at mapped coords). Coordinate mapping 1:1 (world is only 512²; MC's 8:1 would shrink usable nether to 64² — skip). Validate this flow against useMinecraftGame/loadNow mechanics; identify exactly what code changes in the shell.
9. Portal build: obsidian frame (interior min 2×3, like MC), new flint_and_steel item (craft: 1 sliver_ore/ingot? + 1 flint? — no flint exists; simplest craft 1 sliver + 1 coal), used on frame interior → frame validation scan (new helper, bounded) → fill interior with PortalBlock (id ~91, non-solid, emits light ~11, purple animated-ish atlas tile). Portal breaks if frame obsidian broken (check on block change? or lazily when stepping in? — lazily is cheaper: validate frame at travel time, deactivate if broken).
10. Renderer per-dimension environment: a DimensionProfile consumed by GameRenderer + skyView (sky colors constant red-dark for nether, no sun/moon/stars/clouds, fog closer, SKY_LIGHT_FLOOR higher?, daylight forced constant). How does the renderer learn the dimension? (engine snapshot or constructor option.) Nether skylight: cap the world with solid netherrack/bedrock ceiling at top so skylight can't flood; ambient via raised sky-light floor or a nether-specific ambient value.
11. Day/night + spawn gating in nether: dayClock still ticks (shared clock persisted once) but nether daylight pinned (e.g. 0.25) → hostile spawns always on in nether (spawn director keys off daylight — verify this just works), beds refuse (MC: bed explodes — we can just refuse sleep with a toast), weather disabled in nether.
12. WORLDGEN_VERSION: adding generateNetherWorld doesn't change overworld bytes → no bump needed. Nether gets its own SHA-256 baselines in generation tests. BUT wire the missing worldgenVersion discard guard now (both dimensions' diffs discarded together on mismatch — simple and safe). Where exactly does the guard go (WorldSaveGate? openWorld? engine boot?)?
13. Online worlds: ignition (flint&steel on frame) refused when engine authority is server/replica → toast "Portals aren't available in online worlds yet". Where's the cleanest gate — dispatch level or interact level? Server serialize must carry dimensions section through (persist/load round-trip test).

### Stage 3 — Nether content (standard)
14. Worldgen design for generateNetherWorld: netherrack mass with carved caverns, lava seas at a nether lava level (large), glowstone clusters on ceilings, nether ore (post-diamond) veins deep, bedrock-ish floor+ceiling caps (reuse Bedrock block), spawn platform safety (portal arrival must not be inside lava — arrival portal construction clears space). Deterministic via portableSin/hash2D + mulberry32 with fresh xor constants (avoid 0x85ebca6b collision).
15. New blocks (ids from 90 up, sequenced across stages — list exact assignments): Obsidian(90), NetherPortal(91), Netherrack(92), Glowstone(93), NetherOre(94)... plus maybe SoulSand-like? Keep list tight; each needs the full 8-step block checklist.
16. Post-diamond tier: "nether alloy"? name it (e.g. "blazite" or keep simple "nether ore" → "nether ingot"?): smelt nether ore → ingot (furnace recipe w/ coal), tools/sword tier 8 (minePower > diamond, maxDurability higher), maybe armor? (standard scope says tools/weapon upgrade — decide armor in/out; lean: sword+pickaxe+axe only, skip armor to keep sprite work bounded).

# Nether Dimension Epic — Implementation Plan

Branch `feat/nether` off main. One PR. Every commit passes `bun run lint && bun test` (worldgen baseline tests prove overworld bytes never move).

## Validation results that shape the plan (deltas from your leanings)

1. **Travel flow is feasible exactly as sketched, with one ordering trap.** `useMinecraftGame.ts` (`/Users/hutusi/workspace/ai/david/monecraft/lib/game/useMinecraftGame.ts`) drains engine events in the rAF clock (line 451+); `loadNow` (671) is the template: set `skipUnmountSaveRef` → write → `onReloadWorld()`. **Trap:** the 15s autosave and the unmount save both call `persistGame(engine…)` with the *pre-travel* state; the save store is queued latest-wins, so the travel handler must set `skipUnmountSaveRef.current = true` **before** enqueuing the travel save (the flag gates both autosave at line 410 and flush at 426). The remount's `WorldSaveGate` read is ordered after the write by the store (read-your-writes, documented at GameShell.tsx:114-121).
2. **The engine can learn its dimension from the save alone** — no GameShell/WorldMeta plumbing needed. Boot resolves `save.players[local].dimension ?? "overworld"`; fresh worlds are overworld. `GameEngineOptions.dimension` is added only as a test override.
3. **Spawn gating "just works" as hoped**: `tickHostileSpawnDirector` gates on `state.daylight >= HOSTILE_SPAWN_BELOW_DAYLIGHT` (0.28, spawnDirector.ts:255); daylight burn gates on `> 0.72` (mobAI.ts:555); sleep allows `< 0.28` (interact.ts:273). Pinning nether daylight at **0.22** gives always-on hostile spawns and no burn — **but beds would then permit sleep**, so `interactBed` needs an explicit dimension refusal (new `sleepDenied` reason `"dimension"`).
4. **Big landmine you didn't flag: `surfaceYAt`/`highestSolidY` in a roofed world.** `createSurfaceYAt` (spawn.ts:6) returns the *ceiling cap* for every nether column — `randomLandPointNear`, `forceUnstuck`, `spawnInitialMobs`, and respawn would all place entities **on top of the bedrock roof**. Fortunately the engine funnels everything through one field (`this.surfaceYAt`, GameEngine.ts:293), so a nether-aware `createNetherFloorYAt` swapped at boot fixes all consumers at one seam. It must also treat lava floors as invalid (return 1, rejected by the `y > 2` guard in `randomLandPointNear`).
5. **Portal block collision**: `VoxelWorld.isSolid` is `block !== Air && block !== Water` (voxelWorld.ts:56) — `NetherPortal` must join that exclusion, plus the meshing face-cull special case at meshing.ts:311 (`Water || Glass` → add portal), plus refusal in the mining target check (mining.ts:150 currently refuses only Bedrock/Air).
6. **Renderer profile**: `SKY_LIGHT_FLOOR` is baked into the shader string at material construction (GameRenderer.ts:35, 48-60). Since swap-on-travel rebuilds the renderer per dimension, the clean fix is `GameRenderer.create(node, profile)` — the call site (useMinecraftGame.ts:354) already has `ctx.engine` in hand to derive the profile. No uniforms needed.
7. **Server pass-through is nearly free**: `Room` boots `new GameEngine({save: record.save, …})` and `persist()` gzips `engine.serialize()` (room.ts:413-420). An engine-held pass-through field round-trips the nether section with zero room changes. `buildWorldSync` doesn't touch it, so protocol v3 is genuinely untouched.
8. **Projectiles**: `ProjectileState` (state.ts:153) has no `kind`; `spawnArrow` is the single launch path shared by skeleton AI (mobAI.ts:166). Add optional `kind?: "arrow" | "fireball"` + a `projectileKind` on `MobTemplate`; `projectileVisuals.ts` branches on it. Nether mobs are SP-only so the field never crosses the wire.
9. **Stacking**: `maxStackSizeForItem` is `maxDurability ? 1 : MAX_STACK_SIZE` (items.ts:342) — no per-item stack size exists. Add optional `ItemDef.stackSize` honored there (`def.stackSize ?? …`): `bucket` 16, filled buckets 1. Small, clean, testable.
10. **Worldgen guard**: confirmed `worldgenVersion` lives only on `WorldMeta` (worlds.ts:34) and is compared nowhere. Best wiring: stamp it **into the save** at v18 (`SaveData.worldgenVersion`) and guard in the GameEngine constructor via a `save.ts` helper — one seam that covers SP, cloud saves, and the server room. v17→v18 migration leaves it `undefined` (grandfathered — same behavior as today; discarding those diffs blind would be catastrophic).

## Save schema v18 (the first heart)

In types.ts:

```ts
export type DimensionId = "overworld" | "nether";   // in lib/game/types.ts (imported by save/engine/render without cycles)

export type DimensionSection = {
  changes: Array<[number, number]>;
  blockEntities?: SavedContainer[];
  lootedChests?: number[];
  mobs?: SavedMob[];
  vehicles?: SavedVehicle[];
};

export type SaveDataV17 = /* freeze current SaveData shape, following the v16 pattern */;

export type SaveData = Omit<SaveDataV17, "version"> & {
  version: 18;
  /** Stamped by serialize(); absent on migrated saves (grandfathered — guard inert). */
  worldgenVersion?: number;
  /** Non-overworld world-halves. Top-level fields REMAIN the overworld's. */
  dimensions?: { nether?: DimensionSection };
};
// SavedPlayer gains:
//   dimension?: DimensionId;                          // default "overworld"
//   portalArrival?: { x: number; y: number; z: number }; // one-shot, consumed at boot
```

**Design decision (answers Q6):** top-level fields stay the overworld's — no migration of data, no double-writing. `migrateSaveV17toV18` is just the version stamp. The server room engine (always overworld) serializes top-level exactly as today and re-emits `dimensions` verbatim.

Engine plumbing:
- `GameEngine` gains `readonly dimension: DimensionId` (also on `GameState` for systems/renderer) and `private readonly foreignDimensions` — captured at boot:
  - overworld engine: `save?.dimensions` (pass-through, re-emitted in `serialize()`),
  - nether engine: the top-level world-half fields captured verbatim (`changes/blockEntities/lootedChests/mobs/vehicles/villagesSeeded`) and re-emitted top-level, with `dimensions: { nether: <live state> }`.
- `save.ts` helper: `dimensionSectionOf(save: SaveData, dim: DimensionId): DimensionSection` (maps top-level fields for `"overworld"`), used by the constructor's restore path so restore code stays dimension-agnostic.
- `applyWorldgenGuard(save: SaveData): SaveData` in save.ts: if `save.worldgenVersion` is a finite number and `!== WORLDGEN_VERSION`, return the save with the whole world half discarded (`changes: []`, `blockEntities: []`, `lootedChests: []`, `mobs: []`, `vehicles: []`, `dimensions: undefined`, `villagesSeeded: undefined` so villages re-seed) — players kept (`forceUnstuck` and the Bed-check respawn fallback already handle stale positions/spawnPoints). Called first thing in the GameEngine constructor (`options.save ? applyWorldgenGuard(options.save) : null`) — covers SP, cloud, and server room in one seam. This wires the documented-but-missing discard rule (config.ts:406-408).
- `serialize()` writes `version: 18`, `worldgenVersion: WORLDGEN_VERSION`, `players[].dimension = this.state.dimension`, never writes `portalArrival`.
- **New:** `serializeForTravel(target: DimensionId, anchor: {x,y,z}): SaveData` — `serialize()` then rewrite the local player entry: `dimension: target`, `position: anchor`, `portalArrival: anchor`.

Version-assert updates in the same commit as the bump: `save.test.ts` (~7 sites), `e2e/smoke.e2e.ts:294`, plus new round-trip tests. Menu tests' `worldgenVersion: 11` are untouched (no bump this epic).

- `ProjectileState.kind?: "arrow" | "fireball"`, `SpawnArrowOptions.kind`, `MobTemplate.projectileKind?`; mobAI's ranged fire passes it; projectileVisuals renders fireballs as a small emissive orange cube; arrowHit audio branches for a fire "whump".
- spawnDirector dimension-awareness: `tickHostileSpawnDirector` kind list `state.dimension === "nether" ? ["imp","scorcher"] : [...]`; `spawnInitialMobs` nether branch (imps 6 + scorchers 4 around the arrival anchor, no passives/fish/villagers); `tickAquaticSpawnDirector` fails closed naturally (no water). Daylight-pinning makes spawning perpetual (validated). Overworld daylight burn is moot (they can't cross) — no special-casing.
- Tests: template integrity, scorcher fires fireball-kind projectiles, nether director spawns only nether kinds, imp melee parity with zombie tests.

### Commit 5 — `feat(game): nether advancements`
Four rows in `ADVANCEMENTS` + `recordEvent` stats: `hot_tourist` "We Need to Go Deeper" (stat `nether_entered` bumped on the `dimensionTravel` event — emit-time stat recording lands before `serializeForTravel` snapshots it, verified ordering; icon `obsidian`, Adventure), `let_there_be_light` (glowstone mined, Mining), `fire_fighter` (scorcher killed — kind-specific kill stat per the drowned precedent, Combat), `blazing_edge` (blazite tool crafted via `crafted` recipeId prefix, Crafting). Tests in advancements.test.ts.

### Commit 6 — `docs: nether epic` 
manual.md (nether survival guide), reference.md (blocks/items/mobs/recipes tables), tuning.md (portal + nether dials), adding-content.md (new-dimension seam checklist), testing.md map, CHANGELOG epic entry ("save v17→v18, worldgen 11 unchanged, protocol v3 unchanged").

**Final gate:** full `bun test`, lint, typecheck, e2e suite, manual playthrough of the whole loop (mine obsidian via bucket → frame → ignite → travel → mine blazite → tool up → return), then PR.

---

## Risks, ranked

1. **Travel-save race** — autosave/unmount/flush all serialize pre-travel state; the skip-flag-before-write ordering is the whole defense. Add a unit test on the hook if feasible, and the e2e travel test covers it end-to-end.
2. **surfaceYAt ceiling landmine** — any consumer missed (search all `surfaceYAt`/`highestSolidY` call sites; `randomLandPoint`'s hardcoded fallback `y=12` is fine, `isDrySurface` needs a lava-check twin) puts entities on the roof or in lava.
3. **Foreign-dimension pass-through drift** — a future field added to serialize() but not to `DimensionSection` silently stays overworld-global. Mitigate with a doc note in save-format.md and the byte-equal pass-through test.
4. **Frame/portal-block state divergence** — the break-hook + travel-time revalidation must together guarantee no travel through a broken frame; the test matrix in stage 2 commit 3 is the guard.
5. **Worldgen guard false positives** — guard must never fire on `worldgenVersion === undefined`; test explicitly, or one release nukes every migrated world's builds.
6. **Baseline discipline** — nether gen lives in its own module with its own PRNG streams; if `generation.test.ts` ever reddens during this epic, the change is wrong, full stop.

### Critical Files for Implementation
- /Users/hutusi/workspace/ai/david/monecraft/lib/game/engine/GameEngine.ts — dimension boot fork, foreign-section pass-through, serialize/serializeForTravel, ignition gate
- /Users/hutusi/workspace/ai/david/monecraft/lib/game/useMinecraftGame.ts — travel event handling, save-then-remount ordering, renderer profile injection
- /Users/hutusi/workspace/ai/david/monecraft/lib/game/save.ts — v18 migration, dimensionSectionOf, applyWorldgenGuard, field validators
- /Users/hutusi/workspace/ai/david/monecraft/lib/game/engine/systems/interact.ts — bucket branches, bed dimension refusal (plus new sibling systems/portal.ts)
- /Users/hutusi/workspace/ai/david/monecraft/lib/game/render/GameRenderer.ts — DimensionProfile consumption, skyLightFloor, celestial/precip gating

content.text:
I've validated all the load-bearing assumptions (travel flow, serialize/parseSave, spawn gating, projectiles, lighting, meshing solidity, server persist). Everything checks out, with a handful of corrections and traps I found along the way. Here is the plan.

# Nether Dimension Epic — Implementation Plan

Branch `feat/nether` off main. One PR. Every commit passes `bun run lint && bun test` (worldgen baseline tests prove overworld bytes never move).

## Validation results that shape the plan (deltas from your leanings)

1. **Travel flow is feasible exactly as sketched, with one ordering trap.** `useMinecraftGame.ts` (`/Users/hutusi/workspace/ai/david/monecraft/lib/game/useMinecraftGame.ts`) drains engine events in the rAF clock (line 451+); `loadNow` (671) is the template: set `skipUnmountSaveRef` → write → `onReloadWorld()`. **Trap:** the 15s autosave and the unmount save both call `persistGame(engine…)` with the *pre-travel* state; the save store is queued latest-wins, so the travel handler must set `skipUnmountSaveRef.current = true` **before** enqueuing the travel save (the flag gates both autosave at line 410 and flush at 426). The remount's `WorldSaveGate` read is ordered after the write by the store (read-your-writes, documented at GameShell.tsx:114-121).
2. **The engine can learn its dimension from the save alone** — no GameShell/WorldMeta plumbing needed. Boot resolves `save.players[local].dimension ?? "overworld"`; fresh worlds are overworld. `GameEngineOptions.dimension` is added only as a test override.
3. **Spawn gating "just works" as hoped**: `tickHostileSpawnDirector` gates on `state.daylight >= HOSTILE_SPAWN_BELOW_DAYLIGHT` (0.28, spawnDirector.ts:255); daylight burn gates on `> 0.72` (mobAI.ts:555); sleep allows `< 0.28` (interact.ts:273). Pinning nether daylight at **0.22** gives always-on hostile spawns and no burn — **but beds would then permit sleep**, so `interactBed` needs an explicit dimension refusal (new `sleepDenied` reason `"dimension"`).
4. **Big landmine you didn't flag: `surfaceYAt`/`highestSolidY` in a roofed world.** `createSurfaceYAt` (spawn.ts:6) returns the *ceiling cap* for every nether column — `randomLandPointNear`, `forceUnstuck`, `spawnInitialMobs`, and respawn would all place entities **on top of the bedrock roof**. Fortunately the engine funnels everything through one field (`this.surfaceYAt`, GameEngine.ts:293), so a nether-aware `createNetherFloorYAt` swapped at boot fixes all consumers at one seam. It must also treat lava floors as invalid (return 1, rejected by the `y > 2` guard in `randomLandPointNear`).
5. **Portal block collision**: `VoxelWorld.isSolid` is `block !== Air && block !== Water` (voxelWorld.ts:56) — `NetherPortal` must join that exclusion, plus the meshing face-cull special case at meshing.ts:311 (`Water || Glass` → add portal), plus refusal in the mining target check (mining.ts:150 currently refuses only Bedrock/Air).
6. **Renderer profile**: `SKY_LIGHT_FLOOR` is baked into the shader string at material construction (GameRenderer.ts:35, 48-60). Since swap-on-travel rebuilds the renderer per dimension, the clean fix is `GameRenderer.create(node, profile)` — the call site (useMinecraftGame.ts:354) already has `ctx.engine` in hand to derive the profile. No uniforms needed.
7. **Server pass-through is nearly free**: `Room` boots `new GameEngine({save: record.save, …})` and `persist()` gzips `engine.serialize()` (room.ts:413-420). An engine-held pass-through field round-trips the nether section with zero room changes. `buildWorldSync` doesn't touch it, so protocol v3 is genuinely untouched.
8. **Projectiles**: `ProjectileState` (state.ts:153) has no `kind`; `spawnArrow` is the single launch path shared by skeleton AI (mobAI.ts:166). Add optional `kind?: "arrow" | "fireball"` + a `projectileKind` on `MobTemplate`; `projectileVisuals.ts` branches on it. Nether mobs are SP-only so the field never crosses the wire.
9. **Stacking**: `maxStackSizeForItem` is `maxDurability ? 1 : MAX_STACK_SIZE` (items.ts:342) — no per-item stack size exists. Add optional `ItemDef.stackSize` honored there (`def.stackSize ?? …`): `bucket` 16, filled buckets 1. Small, clean, testable.
10. **Worldgen guard**: confirmed `worldgenVersion` lives only on `WorldMeta` (worlds.ts:34) and is compared nowhere. Best wiring: stamp it **into the save** at v18 (`SaveData.worldgenVersion`) and guard in the GameEngine constructor via a `save.ts` helper — one seam that covers SP, cloud saves, and the server room. v17→v18 migration leaves it `undefined` (grandfathered — same behavior as today; discarding those diffs blind would be catastrophic).

1. **Travel-save race** — the `skipUnmountSaveRef.current = true` BEFORE the write is the whole defense (gates autosave L410 + flush L426). Covered by e2e travel test.

3. **Foreign-section drift** — future serialize() fields not added to DimensionSection stay silently overworld-global; doc note + byte-equal pass-through test mitigate.
4. **Frame/portal divergence** — break-hook flood-clear + travel-time revalidation together guarantee no travel through broken frames.
5. **Worldgen-guard false positive** — must be inert on `worldgenVersion === undefined` or one release nukes every migrated world's builds; explicit test.
6. **Baseline discipline** — if `generation.test.ts` reddens at any commit, the change is wrong, full stop.

export const WORLD_SIZE_X = 512;
export const WORLD_SIZE_Y = 150;
export const WORLD_SIZE_Z = 512;

export const enum BlockId {
  Air = 0,
  Grass = 1,
  Dirt = 2,
  Stone = 3,
  Wood = 4,
  Leaves = 5,
  Bedrock = 6,
  Planks = 7,
  Cobblestone = 8,
  Sand = 9,
  Brick = 10,
  Glass = 11,
  SliverOre = 12,
  RubyOre = 13,
  GoldOre = 14,
  SapphireOre = 15,
  DiamondOre = 16,
  Water = 17,
  Snow = 18,
  Cactus = 19,
  Bed = 20,
  Farmland = 21,
  // Wheat growth stages — consecutive ids so a crop advances by +1 (see randomTicks.ts).
  WheatStage0 = 22,
  WheatStage1 = 23,
  WheatStage2 = 24,
  WheatStage3 = 25,
  Furnace = 26,
  Chest = 27,
  // Dungeon blocks (worldgen-only flavor + the spawner block-entity marker).
  MossyCobblestone = 28,
  Spawner = 29,
  // Wood doors — 16 contiguous ids (4 facings × open/closed × lower/upper).
  // doors.ts derives state by offset from DoorNorthLower, so keep them in order.
  DoorNorthLower = 30,
  DoorNorthUpper = 31,
  DoorEastLower = 32,
  DoorEastUpper = 33,
  DoorSouthLower = 34,
  DoorSouthUpper = 35,
  DoorWestLower = 36,
  DoorWestUpper = 37,
  DoorNorthOpenLower = 38,
  DoorNorthOpenUpper = 39,
  DoorEastOpenLower = 40,
  DoorEastOpenUpper = 41,
  DoorSouthOpenLower = 42,
  DoorSouthOpenUpper = 43,
  DoorWestOpenLower = 44,
  DoorWestOpenUpper = 45,
  // A placeable light source: a solid block that emits block light (see lighting.ts).
  Torch = 46,
  // A worldgen-only hazard: a solid, unmineable block that emits max block light
  // and burns the player on contact (see lighting.ts, playerStats.ts).
  Lava = 47,
  // A shallow, common ore: mineable with a wood pickaxe, drops coal (furnace fuel).
  CoalOre = 48,
  // A placeable explosive: right-click with a torch to ignite a fuse, then it blows.
  Tnt = 49,
  // A young tree: plant on grass/dirt, grows into a tree over time (random ticks)
  // or instantly with bone meal. A solid cube like wheat (see atlas.ts).
  Sapling = 50,
  // A crafted station: right-click to open its brewing recipes (potions). Like
  // the furnace, it gates `station: "brewing"` recipes (see interact.ts).
  BrewingStand = 51,
  // A crafted station: right-click to open the enchanting panel, where XP levels
  // are spent to enchant the held tool/weapon/armor (see interact.ts).
  EnchantingTable = 52,
  // A crafted station: right-click to open the anvil panel, where XP levels are
  // spent to repair, combine, or rename the held gear (see interact.ts).
  Anvil = 53,
  // A crafted station: right-click to open the grindstone panel, which strips a
  // held item's enchantments and refunds some XP (see interact.ts).
  Grindstone = 54,
  // Ocean flora. Kelp is a solid cube painted to read as a plant (like wheat)
  // that generates in stalks on the ocean floor and grows upward through water
  // via random ticks; breaking one cell breaks the stalk above it (mining.ts).
  Kelp = 55,
  // Decorative reef blocks scattered on the ocean floor (worldgen only).
  CoralPink = 56,
  CoralBlue = 57,
  // Redstone-lite (see redstone.ts). Power state is id PARITY — even = off,
  // odd = on (`b | 1` / `b & ~1`) — so toggles ride the save diff like doors.
  // Ids 58-67 are floor-mounted "overlays": non-cube, non-colliding shapes
  // meshed via redstoneBounds. The lamp pair is a plain full cube.
  RedstoneWire = 58,
  RedstoneWireOn = 59,
  Lever = 60,
  LeverOn = 61,
  RedstoneButton = 62,
  RedstoneButtonOn = 63,
  PressurePlate = 64,
  PressurePlateOn = 65,
  // The torch item places the LIT variant; the power pass turns it off when
  // its support block is powered (the inverter rule).
  RedstoneTorchOff = 66,
  RedstoneTorch = 67,
  RedstoneLamp = 68,
  RedstoneLampOn = 69,
  // Rails (see rails.ts): flat floor overlays like wire, ridden by minecarts.
  // The powered/detector pairs join the redstone family — power is id PARITY,
  // so each pair MUST start on an even id. Plain Rail carries no power state
  // and must never pass through the redstoneOn/redstoneOff parity math.
  PoweredRail = 70,
  PoweredRailOn = 71,
  DetectorRail = 72,
  DetectorRailOn = 73,
  Rail = 74,
  // Partial building blocks (see slabs.ts). Slabs fill the bottom half of the
  // cell; stairs add a half-height back on the side they FACE, encoded as 4
  // contiguous ids per material (the doors offset-math precedent) in
  // north/east/south/west order — keep them contiguous and in order.
  PlankSlab = 75,
  StoneSlab = 76,
  CobbleSlab = 77,
  PlankStairsNorth = 78,
  PlankStairsEast = 79,
  PlankStairsSouth = 80,
  PlankStairsWest = 81,
  StoneStairsNorth = 82,
  StoneStairsEast = 83,
  StoneStairsSouth = 84,
  StoneStairsWest = 85,
  CobbleStairsNorth = 86,
  CobbleStairsEast = 87,
  CobbleStairsSouth = 88,
  CobbleStairsWest = 89
}

503	/**
504	 * Items a broken block yields. The default is its single `BLOCK_TO_SLOT` entry;
505	 * grass occasionally also drops a seed (the natural seed source), mature wheat
506	 * drops wheat plus 1–2 seeds, and leaves occasionally drop a sapling (their only
507	 * yield — the renewable tree source). `fortuneLevel` (from the Fortune tool used)
508	 * rolls a bonus on **ore** drops only. `rng` is injectable for deterministic tests.
509	 */
510	export function rollBlockDrops(block: BlockId, rng: () => number, fortuneLevel = 0): Array<{ itemId: string; count: number }> {
511	  if (isDoorBlock(block)) return [{ itemId: "door", count: 1 }];
512	  const drops: Array<{ itemId: string; count: number }> = [];
513	  const base = BLOCK_TO_SLOT[block];
514	  if (base) {
515	    let count = 1;
516	    if (fortuneLevel > 0 && FORTUNE_ORE_BLOCKS.has(block)) {
517	      count += Math.floor(rng() * (fortuneLevel * FORTUNE_BONUS_PER_LEVEL + 1));
518	    }
519	    drops.push({ itemId: base, count });
520	  }
521	
522	  if (block === BlockId.Leaves && rng() < LEAVES_SAPLING_DROP_CHANCE) {
523	    drops.push({ itemId: "sapling", count: 1 });
524	  }
525	  if (block === BlockId.Grass && rng() < GRASS_SEED_DROP_CHANCE) {

git add -A && git commit -m "feat(items): buckets — carry water and lava

The nether epic needs obsidian, and obsidian needs movable fluids: no
fluid pickup or placement existed anywhere (lava was worldgen-only). A
bucket (3 sliver ore) scoops the aimed fluid block and pours it back out
via the held-item-use seam, riding the blockChanges.set chokepoint so
lighting (lava's max emission) and remeshing come along for free.

Design choices worth recording:
- Static fluids, no flow simulation: scooping mid-ocean leaves a hole.
  Flow is out of scope for the epic and nothing here precludes it later.
- The solid raycast passes through water (it treats water as empty), so
  the water scoop reuses waterSurfaceRaycast — the fishing-bobber path —
  while lava, a solid block, is hit by the normal raycast.
- New ItemDef.stackSize caps a stack per item (empty buckets bundle to
  16, a filled bucket is a single sloshing payload); durable gear keeps
  its stack-of-1 rule.
- A pour that would entomb the player rolls back, mirroring the
  placeSelectedBlock self-entombment rule (lava is a solid block).
- The fill/empty swap verifies the result actually fit — positive
  adjustSlotCount is best-effort — and refuses rather than losing items
  when the inventory is full." && git log --oneline -1

# Changelog

All notable changes to this project are documented in this file.

## [Unreleased]

### Added

- **Slabs & stairs — half-blocks for real architecture**: craft **slabs** (3 planks/stone/cobble → 6, filling the bottom half of a cell) and **stairs** (6 → 4, a slab plus a raised back that faces away from you when placed — turned by your look direction, so you walk straight up what you just laid; every facing drops the one item). They are the game's first **partial solids**: one set of shape boxes drives both the mesh and a new partial-height collision, so you stand exactly where the block looks like it holds you. Half-blocks count as ground for mobs (a slab floor reads at its real half height) but are **not** valid support for floor-mounted fittings — doors, redstone components, and rails all refuse them. BlockIds 75–89 appended, craft-only: **no save-format or worldgen change**.
- **Auto step-up — half-height rises no longer need a jump**: grounded walking now climbs rises up to `STEP_UP_HEIGHT` (0.55) automatically — up a slab, up each half of a stair, along any half-high terrain lip — while **full blocks still require the jump** (Minecraft parity; the dial is in `config.ts`). This is a deliberate global movement-feel change, not just a slabs feature: it applies anywhere a half-height edge occurs. Airborne and flying movement never auto-steps, the crouch edge-guard is unchanged, and online play needs no protocol or server-clamp change (the pose clamp's existing vertical slack covers the per-tick rise).
- **The drowned — night oceans bite back**: the water gets its first hostile. ### Materials

Crafting ingredients with no direct use on their own: **Wool**, **Feather**,
**Bone**, **Leather**, **String** (mob drops), and **Wheat Seeds** / **Wheat**
(from farming and grass). **Bone Meal** (ground from a bone, 1 → 3) is a
fertilizer: right-click it on a sapling to grow the tree instantly, or on
immature wheat to advance it 1–2 stages. Fuels: **Coal** (mined from coal ore)
and **Charcoal** (smelted from wood) — interchangeable for smelting and torches.
**Gunpowder** (creeper drop) crafts TNT. **Emerald** is the villager [trading](#trading) currency.
Ranged/endgame materials: **Arrow** (bow ammo),
**Cursed Totem** (right-click to summon the boss), and **Dragon Heart** (the
boss drop that crafts the Dragon Sword). The **Treasure Map** (found in
shipwrecks, rarely fished up) shows a compass to the nearest unearthed
[buried treasure](#buried-treasure) while held. Brewing materials: the **Glass Bottle**
and the five **potions** drink with `F` for a [status effect](#status-effects).

## Dungeons

Small cobblestone rooms (speckled with mossy cobble) generate **underground**,
well clear of the spawn area. Each holds 1–2 **loot chests** and a central **mob
spawner**. The loot tables live in `lib/game/dungeonLoot.ts`; a chest fills on
first open or break, with loot seeded so it's the same until you reach it.

Each chest rolls a tier:

| Tier   | Odds | Contents                                                                                                                      |
| ------ | ---- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Common | 75%  | Bone (always), bread, cooked chicken, string, seeds, sliver/gold ore, an occasional stone pickaxe                             |
| Rare   | 25%  | Everything a common chest rolls **plus** diamond/sapphire ore, a ruby/sapphire sword, helmet/chestplate, rare diamond pickaxe |

76	- Design the sound by ear in the [ZZFX designer](https://killedbyapixel.github.io/ZzFX/), then transcribe the parameters into a `SoundDef` in `lib/game/audio/soundParams.ts` using the named-field `zz({...})` helper (field order matches the designer's positional array).
77	- Coverage is pinned: `materials.test.ts` and `soundParams.test.ts` fail on missing material/mob rows, and routing is testable headlessly with the fake `SynthBackend` pattern in `audioDirector.test.ts`. Actual sound quality is a manual `bun run dev` pass.
78	
79	## An interactive block (right-click behavior)
80	
81	- Right-click (and KeyE) dispatch `placeBlock`, which runs a fixed precedence in `GameEngine.dispatch` before falling through to placement: feed an aimed mob → `tryInteractBlock` → use the held item → place. To make a block do something on right-click, register it in `INTERACTIVE_BLOCKS` and add a branch in `tryInteractBlock` (`lib/game/engine/systems/interact.ts`).
82	- The handler returns `true` to consume the click (no block is placed) — return `true` even when the action is refused (e.g. a bed during the day) so the player doesn't place a block into the bed by accident.
83	- Four reference implementations: the **door** atomically toggles matching upper/lower state IDs; the **bed** sets `state.spawnPoint` and starts the sleep fade (`state.sleepTimer`); the **furnace** opens the inventory and sets `state.craftingStation`, which unlocks its `station` recipes (see "A new item or recipe"); the **chest** opens the inventory and sets `state.openContainerIndex` (see below). A block that opens the inventory from a mouse click also needs an `openedStation`/`openedContainer` handler in `useMinecraftGame` to release pointer lock. See [architecture.md](architecture.md) for the step order.
84	- **A station with its own panel (not the recipe book)** — the **enchanting table**, the **anvil**, and the **grindstone** are the reference. Their interaction sets `state.craftingStation` to a new id, but that id goes on the **engine/UI** station union (`craftingStation` on `GameState` and `GameSnapshot`, and the `openedStation` event in `state.ts`, plus the `InventoryPanel` `craftingStation` prop) and **not** on `Recipe.station` — so `STATION_LABELS` (keyed off `Recipe.station`) needs no entry. The panel is a dedicated `*Column` component branched in before the recipe book in `InventoryPanel`, acting on the **selected hotbar slot** (`inventory[selectedHotbarSlot]`); its actions are new `Command`s in `commands.ts` handled in `GameEngine.dispatch` (gated on `state.craftingStation === <id>`), each emitting a one-shot event for the audio director. The block itself is **craft-only** (never generated), so adding the `BlockId` at the end of the enum needs **no `WORLDGEN_VERSION` bump** — just `BLOCK_COLORS` (atlas sizing), an atlas paint branch, the exhaustive `GROUP_BY_BLOCK`, and `BREAK_HARDNESS`/item-def/`BLOCK_TO_SLOT`/recipe.
85	
86	## A container block (block-entity storage)
87	
88	- Blocks are bare `BlockId`s, so any block that needs **attached data** (a chest's items) stores it in `state.containers: Map<voxelIndex, InventorySlot[]>`, keyed by `world.index(x,y,z)`. The chest is the reference:
89	  - **Open**: `interactChest` (an `INTERACTIVE_BLOCKS` branch) lazily creates the slot array, sets `state.openContainerIndex`, opens the inventory, and emits `openedContainer`. The snapshot exposes `container`, and `InventoryPanel` renders a second grid; `toggleInventory`/`pause` clear `openContainerIndex`.
90	  - **Move items**: the `moveStack` command swaps a slot across the inventory/chest boundary using the pure `inventory.moveStack` (chest indices offset by `CONTAINER_SLOT_BASE` in `commands.ts`).
91	  - **Place / break**: placing the block (`mining.placeSelectedBlock`) seeds an empty container; breaking it spills the contents into the inventory via `inventory.tryInsertSlots` (all-or-nothing — a break is refused with a `breakBlocked` event when they don't fit).
92	  - **Persist**: `serialize()` writes non-empty containers to `blockEntities` (`save.serializeContainers`); boot restores them (`save.readContainers`) only for indices that still hold the block. This is an **additive save bump** — see [save-format.md](save-format.md).
93	
94	## A random-tick behavior (growth / spread)
95	
96	- Block updates that happen "over time" run through `lib/game/engine/systems/randomTicks.ts`: every `RANDOM_TICK_INTERVAL_SECONDS` it samples `RANDOM_TICK_SAMPLES` columns within `RANDOM_TICK_RADIUS` of the player and runs a handler on each column's top block. Register a `BlockId → handler` in `RANDOM_TICK_HANDLERS`; the handler edits via `state.blockChanges` and sets `state.worldMeshDirty`.
97	- The crop handler is the reference: wheat stage ids are consecutive, so growth is `block + 1`, and the mature stage has no handler so it stops. Because crops are ordinary block edits, they persist for free via the save's block diff — no new save fields.
98	- Other handlers show the range: `growSapling` checks the block below (only soil matures a sapling) then calls the shared `growTreeAt` (`systems/treeGrowth.ts`); `spreadGrass` reads the four face-neighbour columns' top blocks to re-grass exposed dirt. Both ride `blockChanges`, so they need no save changes either.
99	- A growing block also needs the usual block plumbing — a `BlockId` (appended at the end of the enum so saved ids don't shift), `BLOCK_COLORS` + an atlas paint branch (plants reuse the wheat trick: a solid cube painted to read as a plant, so no new geometry), an exhaustive `GROUP_BY_BLOCK` sound entry, and `BREAK_HARDNESS`/`BLOCK_TO_SLOT`/`rollBlockDrops`. A new **material** item (e.g. bone meal) must also get an `ITEM_SPRITE_GRIDS` entry, or the sprite test fails its no-magenta-checker assertion.
100	- Tunables live in `config.ts`; the headless test pattern (a minimal `GameState`, a scripted rng that maps a sample onto a known column) is in `randomTicks.test.ts`. Watch the rng cadence: a handler that draws a variable number of times (e.g. a tree's trunk-height roll) shifts the sampler's `n % 3` pattern, so prefer an explicit sequence over `scriptedRng` for those.
101	
102	## A transient (session-only) entity (projectile, bobber, …)
103	
104	- Entities that exist only at runtime — arrows, thrown spears, the fishing bobber — live in `GameState` as session fields (an array with a `nextId` counter, or a single nullable field like `state.fishing`). They are **never serialized** (left out of `serialize()`), so they vanish on reload and must be cleared in `respawn()`.
105	- Spawn from the held-item action (e.g. `tryFish`/`tryThrowSelectedSpear` in their systems, wired into the `placeBlock`/`attack` precedence in `GameEngine.ts`), advance them in a per-frame `tick*` system called from `GameEngine.step`, and remove them on expiry/collision/cancel.

- The crop handler is the reference: wheat stage ids are consecutive, so growth is `block + 1`, and the mature stage has no handler so it stops. Because crops are ordinary block edits, they persist for free via the save's block diff — no new save fields.
- Other handlers show the range: `growSapling` checks the block below (only soil matures a sapling) then calls the shared `growTreeAt` (`systems/treeGrowth.ts`); `spreadGrass` reads the four face-neighbour columns' top blocks to re-grass exposed dirt. Both ride `blockChanges`, so they need no save changes either.
- A growing block also needs the usual block plumbing — a `BlockId` (appended at the end of the enum so saved ids don't shift), `BLOCK_COLORS` + an atlas paint branch (plants reuse the wheat trick: a solid cube painted to read as a plant, so no new geometry), an exhaustive `GROUP_BY_BLOCK` sound entry, and `BREAK_HARDNESS`/`BLOCK_TO_SLOT`/`rollBlockDrops`. A new **material** item (e.g. bone meal) must also get an `ITEM_SPRITE_GRIDS` entry, or the sprite test fails its no-magenta-checker assertion.
- Tunables live in `config.ts`; the headless test pattern (a minimal `GameState`, a scripted rng that maps a sample onto a known column) is in `randomTicks.test.ts`. Watch the rng cadence: a handler that draws a variable number of times (e.g. a tree's trunk-height roll) shifts the sampler's `n % 3` pattern, so prefer an explicit sequence over `scriptedRng` for those.

## A transient (session-only) entity (projectile, bobber, …)

- Entities that exist only at runtime — arrows, thrown spears, the fishing bobber — live in `GameState` as session fields (an array with a `nextId` counter, or a single nullable field like `state.fishing`). They are **never serialized** (left out of `serialize()`), so they vanish on reload and must be cleared in `respawn()`.
- Spawn from the held-item action (e.g. `tryFish`/`tryThrowSelectedSpear` in their systems, wired into the `placeBlock`/`attack` precedence in `GameEngine.ts`), advance them in a per-frame `tick*` system called from `GameEngine.step`, and remove them on expiry/collision/cancel.

## [Unreleased]

### Added

- **Buckets, movable fluids & obsidian — the nether epic's opening act**: craft a **bucket** (3 sliver ore; empties stack to 16, a filled bucket rides alone) and right-click to **scoop** the aimed water or lava block and **pour** it back out against a solid face — the game's first fluid pickup/placement (lava was worldgen-only and untouchable). Fluids are **still**: no flow simulation, so a scooped ocean cell leaves a neat one-block hole and a poured block stays put; a poured lava block glows (max light) and burns exactly like the native floods, and a pour that would entomb you rolls back like ordinary placement. Pour **water directly onto lava** and it hisses into **obsidian** (BlockId 90, appended) — the game's only obsidian source and its hardest mineable block: **diamond-pickaxe-gated**, hardness 40, deliberately a grind because it is the portal-frame material of the dimension work that follows. Under the hood: a new `ItemDef.stackSize` caps per-item stacks, the water scoop reuses the fishing-bobber `waterSurfaceRaycast` (the solid raycast passes through water), and every mutation rides the ordinary `blockChanges.set` chokepoint — **no save-format, worldgen, or protocol change** (v17 / worldgen 11 / protocol v3 untouched).

1	# Changelog
2	
3	All notable changes to this project are documented in this file.
4	
5	## [Unreleased]
6	
7	### Added
8	
9	- **Slabs & stairs — half-blocks for real architecture**: craft **slabs** (3 planks/stone/cobble → 6, filling the bottom half of a cell) and **stairs** (6 → 4, a slab plus a raised back that faces away from you when placed — turned by your look direction, so you walk straight up what you just laid; every facing drops the one item). They are the game's first **partial solids**: one set of shape boxes drives both the mesh and a new partial-height collision, so you stand exactly where the block looks like it holds you. Half-blocks count as ground for mobs (a slab floor reads at its real half height) but are **not** valid support for floor-mounted fittings — doors, redstone components, and rails all refuse them. BlockIds 75–89 appended, craft-only: **no save-format or worldgen change**.
10	- **Auto step-up — half-height rises no longer need a jump**: grounded walking now climbs rises up to `STEP_UP_HEIGHT` (0.55) automatically — up a slab, up each half of a stair, along any half-high terrain lip — while **full blocks still require the jump** (Minecraft parity; the dial is in `config.ts`). This is a deliberate global movement-feel change, not just a slabs feature: it applies anywhere a half-height edge occurs. Airborne and flying movement never auto-steps, the crouch edge-guard is unchanged, and online play needs no protocol or server-clamp change (the pose clamp's existing vertical slack covers the per-tick rise).

# Changelog

All notable changes to this project are documented in this file.

## [Unreleased]

### Added

- **Slabs & stairs — half-blocks for real architecture**: craft **slabs** (3 planks/stone/cobble → 6, filling the bottom half of a cell) and **stairs** (6 → 4, a slab plus a raised back that faces away from you when placed — turned by your look direction, so you walk straight up what you just laid; every facing drops the one item). They are the game's first **partial solids**: one set of shape boxes drives both the mesh and a new partial-height collision, so you stand exactly where the block looks like it holds you. Half-blocks count as ground for mobs (a slab floor reads at its real half height) but are **not** valid support for floor-mounted fittings — doors, redstone components, and rails all refuse them. BlockIds 75–89 appended, craft-only: **no save-format or worldgen change**.
- **Auto step-up — half-height rises no longer need a jump**: grounded walking now climbs rises up to `STEP_UP_HEIGHT` (0.55) automatically — up a slab, up each half of a stair, along any half-high terrain lip — while **full blocks still require the jump** (Minecraft parity; the dial is in `config.ts`). This is a deliberate global movement-feel change, not just a slabs feature: it applies anywhere a half-height edge occurs. Airborne and flying movement never auto-steps, the crouch edge-guard is unchanged, and online play needs no protocol or server-clamp change (the pose clamp's existing vertical slack covers the per-tick rise).

Under the hood: a new `ItemDef.stackSize` caps per-item stacks, the water scoop reuses the fishing-bobber `waterSurfaceRaycast` (the solid raycast passes through water), and every mutation rides the ordinary `blockChanges.set` chokepoint — **no save-format, worldgen, or protocol change** (v17 / worldgen 11 / protocol v3 untouched).

- **Slabs & stairs — half-blocks for real architecture**: craft **slabs** (3 planks/stone/cobble → 6, filling the bottom half of a cell) and **stairs** (6 → 4, a slab plus a raised back that faces away from you when placed — turned by your look direction, so you walk straight up what you just laid; every facing drops the one item). They are the game's first **partial solids**: one set of shape boxes drives both the mesh and a new partial-height collision, so you stand exactly where the block looks like it holds you. Half-blocks count as ground for mobs (a slab floor reads at its real half height) but are **not** valid support for floor-mounted fittings — doors, redstone components, and rails all refuse them. BlockIds 75–89 appended, craft-only: **no save-format or worldgen change**.

- **Auto step-up — half-height rises no longer need a jump**: grounded walking now climbs rises up to `STEP_UP_HEIGHT` (0.55) automatically — up a slab, up each half of a stair, along any half-high terrain lip — while **full blocks still require the jump** (Minecraft parity; the dial is in `config.ts`). This is a deliberate global movement-feel change, not just a slabs feature: it applies anywhere a half-height edge occurs. Airborne and flying movement never auto-steps, the crouch edge-guard is unchanged, and online play needs no protocol or server-clamp change (the pose clamp's existing vertical slack covers the per-tick rise).

- **The drowned — night oceans bite back**: the water gets its first hostile. At night (difficulty-gated like every hostile; none on Peaceful), sunken teal zombies rise in open water near you — never point-blank under a swimmer — and pursue you through the water in full 3D, striking with the same line-of-sight, difficulty scaling, and knockback rules as a land mob's melee. They are **strictly water-bound**: the same movement gate that keeps fish in the water keeps a drowned from ever walking ashore (knocked onto land, it suffocates like a beached cod), and being submerged shields it from the daylight burn — so a guarded wreck stays guarded until you deal with its keeper. Drops: rotten flesh, a 50% kelp, and a **7% sliver spear** (the trident nod); the first kill unlocks **Revenge of the Tides**. Population is bounded by its own `DROWNED_CAP` inside the shared hostile cap, and the fish top-up now counts only passives so a full night of drowned can't starve the cod schools. No new blocks, no save/worldgen/protocol change — the drowned is a fungible hostile riding the existing mob machinery (recipe-book hints also learned that chance-gated drops aren't an item's "natural source", so the spear keeps its Craft hint).

  (foreignDimensions), so the server room — which always runs the
  overworld — round-trips a world's nether builds through its persist
  cycle without knowing they exist. Pinned by a byte-equality test.

  the long-documented-but-never-implemented staleness rule
  (config.ts/save-format.md): a mismatched stamp discards every
  dimension's world half and reboots from the seed, keeping the players.
  Saves with NO stamp (anything migrated from ≤v17) are grandfathered —
  discarding those blind would wipe every existing world's builds. One
  seam in the constructor covers single-player, cloud saves, and the
  server room alike.

+ * Deterministic spiral search for a safe nether spawn: a floor pocket with

git add -A && git commit -m "feat(engine): dimension-aware boot

The engine now knows which dimension it simulates. Swap-on-travel keeps
one live dimension per engine, so the constructor is the whole fork: the
local player's saved dimension (or a test override) picks the generator
(a stub nether — bedrock-capped stone mass — that the content stage
replaces wholesale), the world half restores from that dimension's save
section via dimensionSectionOf, and serialize() inverts cleanly — a
nether engine re-emits the overworld's half verbatim at the top level
and writes its live state under dimensions.nether. Pinned by a
round-trip test that carries an overworld edit through a nether detour
and back untouched.

The subtle bits this slice defuses:
- surfaceYAt in a ROOFED world: highestSolidY is the bedrock ceiling, so
  unstuck/respawn/spawn-directors would all place entities on the roof.
  createNetherFloorYAt walks each column down to the highest cavern-floor
  pocket (a lava floor is not a floor) and swaps in at the one seam every
  consumer reads.
- Daylight is pinned to NETHER_DAYLIGHT (0.22): under the hostile-spawn
  threshold (perpetual spawns once nether kinds exist) and the burn
  threshold, while the shared day clock keeps ticking. But 0.22 is also
  under the sleep threshold, so beds get an explicit dimension refusal
  rather than skipping to a morning that never comes.
- The overworld spawn rosters (initial groups, hostile director, aquatic
  director) early-return in the nether so zombies don't colonize it
  before the content stage lands its own kinds; weather stays clear.
  All gates compare === \"nether\" so bare test fixtures keep their
  overworld behavior." && git log --oneline -1

/** Sound family of a block — drives break/place/footstep/mining-tick sounds. */
export type MaterialGroup = "stone" | "wood" | "grass" | "sand" | "glass" | "water";

export const MATERIAL_GROUPS: readonly MaterialGroup[] = ["stone", "wood", "grass", "sand", "glass", "water"];

// Exhaustive over BlockId so adding a block without a sound group is a type error.
const GROUP_BY_BLOCK: Record<BlockId, MaterialGroup> = {
  [BlockId.Air]: "grass", // never audible; mapped only for exhaustiveness
  [BlockId.Grass]: "grass",

breaking any frame obsidian also flood-clears the attached surface
immediately via a bounded fill hooked into the mining break path.
