content.content:
1	# Save format & compatibility
2	
3	## Schema
4	
5	`SaveData` (version 17) in `lib/game/types.ts`. Since v17 the per-player
6	fields below (inventory, equipped armor, selected slot, position,
7	hearts/hunger, effects, xp, stats, advancements, spawn point, game mode,
8	gameOver) live inside `players: SavedPlayer[]` — a single `"local"` entry in
9	single-player — while the world-level fields stay top-level (see the v17
10	entry under Version history). The field-by-field contracts are unchanged:
11	
12	- world `seed`
13	- `worldType` (optional) — the generation preset (`"default"` | `"flat"` | `"amplified"` | `"islands"`); absent ⇒ `"default"`. Like `seed`, it is fixed for the world's life and the world must always regenerate with it, since the block-diffs were recorded against that terrain
14	- `gameMode` (optional) — the player's game mode (`"survival"` | `"creative"` | `"adventure"` | `"spectator"`); absent ⇒ `"survival"`. Unlike `worldType`, this is **switchable in-game** (pause menu), so the saved value is the _current_ mode, not the one chosen at creation. Restored by `restoreGameMode` (`lib/game/save.ts`); `isFlying` is session-only and never serialized
15	- `difficulty` (optional) — the player's difficulty (`"peaceful"` | `"easy"` | `"normal"` | `"hard"`); absent ⇒ `"normal"`. An axis orthogonal to `gameMode`, and likewise **switchable in-game** (pause menu), so the saved value is the _current_ difficulty. Restored by `restoreDifficulty` (`lib/game/save.ts`); the per-level multipliers live in `lib/game/difficulties.ts`, the starvation accumulator (`starvationTimer`) is session-only
16	- `hardcore` (optional) — the Hardcore flag (`boolean`); absent ⇒ `false`. **Immutable** (unlike `gameMode`/`difficulty`): a hardcore world is forced to Survival + Hard and the engine locks both switchers. Restored by `restoreHardcore`
17	- `gameOver` (optional) — the permadeath flag (`boolean`); absent ⇒ `false`. Set once a hardcore run has ended in death; a reloaded `gameOver` world boots into the spectator "dead world" state (never playable). Restored by `restoreGameOver`. (The transient `isDead`/`respawnTimer` stay session-only — hardcore death is captured by this flag instead.)
18	- a block **diff** list — `changes: [blockIndex, blockId][]`; edits that revert to the generated baseline are pruned (player-placed crops, beds, furnaces, chests, and both halves/states of doors ride this list — they are ordinary block edits)
19	- inventory slots with durability, **enchantments, and a custom name** (36 slots; the first 9 are the hotbar). Each `SavedSlot` is `{ id, count, durability?, enchantments?, customName? }`; `enchantments` (`{ id, level }[]`) and `customName` (the anvil rename) ride durable gear only and are validated on load (`restoreSlot` — known enchant ids via `Object.hasOwn`, levels clamped to `1..ENCHANT_MAX_LEVEL`; `customName` trimmed and capped to `CUSTOM_NAME_MAX_LEN`, blanks dropped). The same path serializes chest contents
20	- `xp` (optional) — banked experience points (`XP_PER_LEVEL` points = one level). Earned from kills/ore/fishing, spent at the enchanting table. Restored by `restoreXp` (finite, ≥ 0). Unlike effects, XP is a currency and is **kept across death**
21	- equipped armor — the worn pieces themselves (one per slot, dedicated storage), persisted as per-slot `SavedSlot` via `serializeEquippedArmor`/`restoreEquippedArmor` (so worn durability/enchantments/customName survive). A worn piece lives **only** here, not in the 36 inventory slots
22	- selected hotbar slot (0–8)
23	- player position — validated on load by `restorePlayerPosition` (`lib/game/save.ts`): coords keep their fractional part (the player isn't grid-aligned) but a missing or non-finite (NaN/Infinity) position is rejected, leaving the fresh spawn in place so a corrupt blob can't load a broken world or slip past the `position.y < 2` unstuck net
24	- `dayClock`, `hearts`, `hunger` (all optional) — time of day and player stats, so sleeping through the night and a hurt/hungry player survive a reload
25	- `spawnPoint` (optional, `{x,y,z}` or null) — the bed respawn point; respawn falls back to a random land point when it is null or the block there is no longer a bed
26	- `blockEntities` (optional) — chest contents as `{ index, slots }[]`, keyed by the block's voxel index (the same index space as `changes`). Only **non-empty** chests are stored; an empty one carries no data and is recreated empty when opened. On load each entry is kept only if that index still holds a Chest block. This is the first per-block metadata in the format — `lib/game/save.ts` (`serializeContainers` / `readContainers`) handles it
27	- `effects` (optional) — active status effects as `{ id, remaining }[]` (remaining in seconds). Drink-granted buffs (Speed/Strength/Regeneration/Fire Resistance/Water Breathing) and the rotten-flesh Poison hazard live in `state.effects` (a Map) and persist here, but are **cleared on death**, so a saved-then-reloaded world resumes whatever was active at save time. On load, `restoreEffects` (`lib/game/save.ts`) drops unknown ids and non-positive/garbage durations
28	- `lootedChests` (optional) — voxel indices of **worldgen** loot chests (dungeon, shipwreck, or buried treasure) the player has already opened or broken. Worldgen chests' contents are **not** in `changes`/`blockEntities` until accessed; the engine fills them lazily on first access (loot seeded from `world.seed ^ index`, mixed with a per-family constant, from the family's own table) and records the index here. Because an emptied chest drops out of `blockEntities`, this set — not the chest's emptiness — is what prevents a re-roll on reload. The session-only sets of _which_ indices belong to each family are not stored; they are re-derived from the seed each load via `collectDungeonSites` / `collectShipwreckSites` / `collectTreasureSites` (`lib/world/generation.ts`). The field kept its name when shipwrecks/buried treasure generalized it (state-side it is `lootedWorldgenChests`), so pre-aquatic saves read unchanged. Handled by `serializeLootedChests` / `readLootedChests` in `lib/game/save.ts`
29	- `stats` (optional) — gameplay **statistics** as `{ id, value }[]` (blocks mined, mobs killed, items crafted/enchanted, potions drunk, fish caught, distance travelled, time played, …). Counters live in `state.stats` (a `Map<string, number>`) and are folded in at the engine's single emit chokepoint (`recordEvent`/`recordTick`, `lib/game/engine/systems/advancements.ts`). Like `xp` and **unlike `effects`**, they are a long-term record and are **kept across death**. Only positive values are written; `restoreStats` (`lib/game/save.ts`) drops non-string ids and negative/garbage values. The id set is open (per-recipe `crafted_<id>` and per-block `*_mined` counters), so there's no allow-list
30	- `advancements` (optional) — the unlocked **advancement** ids as `string[]`. Unlock is uniform — `state.stats.get(stat) >= threshold` for each declarative entry in `ADVANCEMENTS` (`lib/game/engine/systems/advancements.ts`) — and ids accumulate in `state.advancements` (a `Set`). Also **kept across death**; `restoreAdvancements` (`lib/game/save.ts`) keeps non-empty strings only, de-duplicated. Unknown persisted ids (e.g. a renamed entry) are harmless: they round-trip but never re-unlock, since `evaluateAdvancements` only iterates the registry
31	- `mobs` (optional) — persisted mobs as `SavedMob[]` (`{ kind, x, y, z, hp, faction, owner?, sitting?, ageTimer?, profession? }`). The fungible wild/hostile population is re-seeded each boot by `spawnInitialMobs`, so only mobs matching `isPersistentMob` are written: **tamed pets** (`owner` set) and **village residents** (`faction === "villager"`). `serializeMobs`/`restoreMobs` (`lib/game/save.ts`) round-trip and validate — dropping unknown kinds, non-finite coords, non-positive hp, and anything that isn't a valid persistent shape (an owned ally pet, or an owner-less villager); a resident's `profession` (v15) is validated against the known set. The engine rebuilds each live `MobState` **before** `spawnInitialMobs`, re-grounding `y` onto the current surface (the world may have changed), assigning fresh ids (the renderer reconciles by id from a cold boot), and clamping hp + re-arming a pet's detect range. Like `xp`/`stats` and **unlike `effects`**, persisted mobs are kept across death
32	- `vehicles` (optional) — placed water vehicles as `SavedVehicle[]` (`{ kind, x, y, z, yaw }`, where `kind` is `"raft"` or `"ship"`). The live rider link (`mountedVehicleId` / `VehicleState.rider`) is session-only and never serialized; reloads restore only the placed entities. `serializeVehicles`/`restoreVehicles` (`lib/game/save.ts`) round-trip and validate — dropping unknown kinds and non-finite poses — and the engine only keeps restored vehicles that still sit on valid water support
33	
34	Each world's `SaveData` is stored in **IndexedDB** — database `monecraft`, object store `worldSaves`, keyed by world id (including the synthetic `cloud:<id>` ids) — as a structured clone of the object, not a JSON string, so it lives off localStorage's ~5–10 MB origin quota. The async store is `lib/game/saveStore.ts` (`worldSaves.read/write/remove/flushWrite`) over the minimal wrapper in `lib/game/idbKv.ts`; writes are queued per world with latest-wins coalescing, reads are read-your-writes (a remount can never see a stale blob), and `write()` resolves only when the transaction has durably committed. Validation and the migration chain live in `lib/game/save.ts` — every read (either container) flows through `parseSave`; the sync `readSave`/`writeSave` (injectable `Storage`) remain for the legacy localStorage keys `minecraft_world_save_<worldId>` (`worldSaveKey` in `lib/game/worlds.ts`), which are now only a migration source, the store's fallback when IndexedDB is unavailable (some private modes — old behavior, quota risk included), and the server's save path (`server/persistence.ts`). `GameEngine.serialize()` produces the save from live state, and `lib/game/engine/blockChanges.ts` maintains the block diff. (The legacy single-world key `SAVE_KEY` = `minecraft_save_v7` is read only once, by the migration described under [Profiles & worlds](#profiles--worlds).)
35	
36	Audio volume preferences live under a **separate**, global key (`minecraft_audio_v1`, `lib/game/audio/settings.ts`), shared across all profiles and not part of any world save or its versioning.
37	
38	**Per-voxel light is never serialized.** It is a derived cache (`world.light`), recomputed from the blocks at load by `computeFullLight` and patched locally on every edit (`lib/world/lighting.ts`); the bake reads only `world.blocks`, so the save needs no lighting field.
39	
40	Continuous-water exposure, lava burn, and the oxygen/drowning meter all live only
41	in transient `GameTimers`/state. Saving, reloading, or respawning resets them
42	(breath restores to full). The status-effect **accumulators** (`effectRegenTimer`,
43	`effectPoisonTimer`) are likewise transient — but the effects **themselves**
44	(`state.effects`) persist via the `effects` field above and survive a reload.
45	
46	### Version history
47	
48	- **v17** (the players array — multiplayer groundwork) — every per-player field moves off the top level into `players: SavedPlayer[]`; world-level fields (seed, worldType, difficulty, hardcore, changes, blockEntities, lootedChests, mobs, vehicles, dayClock, villagesSeeded) stay put. `SavedPlayer` keeps the old field names (one rename: the top-level `player` position becomes `position`) so the per-field validators are shared between migration and live restores. `migrateSaveV16toV17` is a pure field move wrapping a flat single-player save as `[{ id: "local", … }]`, and rewrites pet owners from the legacy literal `"player"` to `"local"` — `SavedMob.owner` is a real player id from here on. A single-player world always saves one `"local"` entry; a multiplayer server holds one entry per known account and restores a joining player's slice through the same `restorePlayerFields` mirror that `serialize()` writes. Hardcore's `gameOver` is per-player (`restoreGameOver(save, savedPlayer)` requires the world's `hardcore` flag as before).
49	- **Unreleased (no save bump; `WORLDGEN_VERSION` 10→11)** — **portable worldgen noise**. Every seed-determined noise call (terrain waves, biome fields, cave-walk trig, the underground speckle hash) moved from `Math.sin` — whose results are engine-defined, so the same seed could generate different terrain on different JS engines — to the bit-portable implementations in `lib/world/noise.ts`. Same formulas, near-identical terrain (all structural probes unchanged), but exact bytes shift: old worlds discard stale block-diffs and reboot from their seed, and all worldgen digests were re-baselined into `lib/world/generationBaselines.ts` per docs/testing.md. The save **schema stays v16** — no field changes. This makes seed + block-diff sync portable between a browser and a Bun multiplayer server, and is proven in CI by `e2e/determinism.e2e.ts` (Chromium digest ≡ Bun baseline). Weather windows and the daylight curve moved to the same portable primitives (both transient/derived — no save impact).
50	- **0.12.0 (no save bump; `WORLDGEN_VERSION` 9→10)** — the **aquatic update**. Kelp/coral (`BlockId`s **appended**: 55–57), sunken **shipwrecks**, and **buried treasure** all write generated blocks, so the worldgen baseline bumps 9→10 (old worlds discard stale block-diffs and reboot from their seed; the worldgen/world-type/meshing digests were re-baselined per docs/testing.md). The save **schema stays v16**: cod/salmon are fungible wild mobs (never persisted; `restoreMobs` in older builds drops unknown kinds), kelp growth/harvest rides the block diff, the `treasure_map`/`dried_kelp`/coral items are additive string ids with **no instance state** (the map's compass target is derived from the seed at runtime), and shipwreck/buried chests reuse the persisted `lootedChests` index set unchanged (see above — the fill family is re-derived, not stored).
51	- **v16** (water vehicles) — adds optional top-level `vehicles` (`SavedVehicle[]`) for placed **rafts** and **ships**. `migrateSaveV15toV16` is a pure version bump (absent ⇒ no placed vehicles). Vehicle items are additive string ids; placed vehicles are entities, not voxel blocks, so there is **no `BlockId` or worldgen change** (`WORLDGEN_VERSION` stays 9). The rider/mount state is transient and reloads with the player unmounted.
52	- **v15** (villager professions — Living World, PR 2) — adds an optional `profession` (`"farmer" | "blacksmith" | "librarian" | "cleric"`) on a villager resident's `SavedMob`. `migrateSaveV14toV15` is a pure version bump (absent ⇒ the engine assigns one round-robin at boot). Validated against the known professions on load. **Generated villages** in the same release bump **`WORLDGEN_VERSION` 8→9** (villages add structures, so old block-diffs are stale and discarded — the worldgen/world-type/meshing digests were re-baselined per docs/testing.md); village residents persist via the existing v14 `mobs` field, and **raids** are transient (`state.raid` + raiders aren't serialized, like the boss), so neither needs further save schema beyond the additive `profession` and the by-id Ominous Horn item.
53	- **v14** (persisted mobs — Living World, PR 1) — adds an optional top-level `mobs` (`SavedMob[]`). `migrateSaveV13toV14` is a pure version bump (absent ⇒ no persisted mobs; the world re-seeds its wildlife as before). This is the first mob persistence in the format: `isPersistentMob` keeps only **tamed pets** here (PR-B adds village residents), since the fungible population is re-created each boot. Restored before `spawnInitialMobs`, with `y` re-grounded onto the current surface and fresh ids assigned. The new `faction`/`owner`/`sitting`/`targetId`/`retargetTimer` mob fields are session-side; only the durable ones land in `SavedMob`. The wolf and cat are additive `MobKind`s with no `BlockId`/item changes, so **`WORLDGEN_VERSION` stays at 8** and `SAVE_KEY` is unchanged.
54	- **v13** (advancements & statistics) — adds optional top-level `stats` (`{ id, value }[]`) and `advancements` (`string[]`). `migrateSaveV12toV13` is a pure version bump (both absent ⇒ no stats, no advancements yet earned). Both are progression meta folded in at the engine's single emit chokepoint and, like `xp` and **unlike `effects`**, are **kept across death** (`clearEffects` never touches them). `serializeStats`/`restoreStats` and `restoreAdvancements` (`lib/game/save.ts`) round-trip and validate them. No new `BlockId`, no new item, and no worldgen change — advancement icons reuse existing item/block sprites — so **`WORLDGEN_VERSION` stays at 8** and `SAVE_KEY` is unchanged.
55	- **Unreleased (no save bump)** — new enchantments (**Power**, **Punch**, **Knockback**, **Looting**, **Fortune**, **Feather Falling**) ride the existing per-slot `enchantments` field, and new status effects (**Haste**, **Resistance**, **Jump Boost**) ride the existing top-level `effects` field. Their ids are added to the save validators' known-id sets (`VALID_ENCHANT_IDS` / `VALID_EFFECT_IDS`, both compile-enforced `Record<…, true>`). No new field, no new `BlockId`, no worldgen change — the save schema stays **v12** and **`WORLDGEN_VERSION` stays at 8** (the same additive-id pattern as Mending). Older builds silently drop unknown ids on load.
56	- **v12** (dedicated armor storage) — fixes a bug where equipped armor stayed in the inventory and occupied a hotbar/storage slot. `equippedArmor` is no longer a by-id reference into `inventorySlots` but the worn pieces themselves, persisted per slot as `SavedSlot` (via `serializeEquippedArmor`/`restoreEquippedArmor`, reusing the shared `restoreSlot` validation). `migrateSaveV11toV12` moves each legacy by-id equip out of `inventorySlots` into the armor record (preserving durability/enchantments/customName; equips whose item isn't found or isn't valid armor are dropped; a legacy `inventoryCounts`-only save just drops the equip map and keeps the items). No worldgen change — **`WORLDGEN_VERSION` stays at 8** and `SAVE_KEY` is unchanged.
57	- **v11** (anvil rename & Mending) — adds an optional `customName` on each `SavedSlot` (the anvil rename). `migrateSaveV10toV11` is a pure version bump (absent ⇒ no custom name). `customName` rides the existing `inventorySlotsSnapshot`/`restoreSlot` path (shared by inventory and chests), is restored on durable gear only, and is trimmed + capped to `CUSTOM_NAME_MAX_LEN` with blanks dropped. The **Mending** enchantment adds no new field — it rides the existing per-slot `enchantments` (and its `mending` id is added to the save validator's known-id set). The **Anvil** and **Grindstone** items save by string id and their `BlockId`s are **appended** so saved block ids never shift. No worldgen change — both are craft-only — so **`WORLDGEN_VERSION` stays at 8**.
58	- **v10** (Hardcore) — adds optional top-level `hardcore` and `gameOver` booleans. `migrateSaveV9toV10` is a pure version bump (both absent ⇒ a normal, non-hardcore world, via `restoreHardcore`/`restoreGameOver`). `hardcore` is immutable (forces Survival + Hard, locks both switchers); `gameOver` is the persisted permadeath flag, so a dead hardcore world reloads into its spectator state rather than respawning (the transient `isDead`/`respawnTimer` remain session-only). No worldgen change — so **`WORLDGEN_VERSION` stays at 8**.
59	- **v9** (difficulty) — adds an optional top-level `difficulty` (`"peaceful"` | `"easy"` | `"normal"` | `"hard"`). `migrateSaveV8toV9` is a pure version bump (absent ⇒ `"normal"`, via `restoreDifficulty`). Difficulty is an axis orthogonal to `gameMode`, switchable in-game, so the _current_ level is what's stored; the per-level multipliers live in `lib/game/difficulties.ts` and the `starvationTimer` accumulator is session-only. No worldgen change — difficulty touches no generation — so **`WORLDGEN_VERSION` stays at 8**.
60	- **v8** (game modes) — adds an optional top-level `gameMode` (`"survival"` | `"creative"` | `"adventure"` | `"spectator"`). `migrateSaveV7toV8` is a pure version bump (absent ⇒ `"survival"`, via `restoreGameMode`). The mode is switchable in-game, so the _current_ mode is what's stored; the transient `isFlying` is never serialized. No worldgen change — modes touch no generation — so **`WORLDGEN_VERSION` stays at 8**.
61	- **v7** (XP & enchanting) — adds optional top-level `xp` and an optional `enchantments` array on each `SavedSlot`. `migrateSaveV6toV7` is a pure version bump (absent → xp 0, no enchantments). XP persists and is **kept across death** (it's a currency, not a status effect); enchantments ride the existing `inventorySlotsSnapshot`/`restoreSlot` path (shared by inventory and chests) and are validated on load. The **Enchanting Table** item saves by string id and the `EnchantingTable` `BlockId` is **appended** (id 52) so saved block ids never shift. No worldgen change — **`WORLDGEN_VERSION` stays at 8**.
62	- **v6** (status effects, brewing & potions) — adds optional `effects` (`{ id, remaining }[]`). `migrateSaveV5toV6` is a pure version bump (absent → no active effects), so pre-effect saves load clean. Effects persist but are cleared on death; `serializeEffects`/`restoreEffects` (`lib/game/save.ts`) round-trip and validate them. Potions, glass bottles, and the **Brewing Stand** item save by string id; the `BrewingStand` `BlockId` is **appended at the end** of the enum (id 51) so existing saved block ids never shift, and a placed stand persists in the block diff like any block. No worldgen change — the new effects/recipes touch no generation — so **`WORLDGEN_VERSION` stays at 8** and the determinism hashes are untouched.
63	- **v5** (unchanged for fishing) — the active cast is the session-only `state.fishing` field (a transient bobber, like in-flight arrows and thrown spears); it is never serialized and is cleared on respawn. The fishing rod and raw/cooked fish are additive items saved by string id, and a catch is an ordinary inventory change. No worldgen change, so neither the `version` nor `WORLDGEN_VERSION` moved.
64	- **v5** (unchanged for the living world — saplings, bone meal & grass spread) — every effect is an ordinary block edit that rides the `changes` diff: a planted sapling, a grown tree's wood and leaves, and re-grassed dirt all persist with no new fields, and bone meal is an additive item saved by string id. The `Sapling` `BlockId` is **appended at the end** of the enum (id 50) so existing saved block ids never shift. Crucially, the runtime tree grower (`systems/treeGrowth.ts`) shares **no** code with worldgen's hash-pinned `placeTrees`, so the generated terrain is byte-identical and **neither the `version` nor `WORLDGEN_VERSION` moved**.
65	- **v5** (unchanged for villagers & trading) — the villager mob is transient like every mob, and trading needs no persisted state: a trade is a station-gated recipe (`station: "villager"`) run through the existing `craft` command, the open trade station (`craftingStation`) is session-only, and there are no per-trade use caps to store. **Emerald** and any traded goods save by string id in the existing inventory slots. No worldgen change (villagers spawn into the passive population; there are no village structures), so neither the `version` nor `WORLDGEN_VERSION` moved.
66	- **v5** (unchanged for creepers & TNT) — the creeper mob, gunpowder, and the explosion system add no persisted state: mobs are transient, **a creeper's lit fuse and a primed TNT block's countdown are session-only** (`MobState.fuseTimer` and `state.primedTnt` are never serialized — like the boss and in-flight arrows). Gunpowder and the TNT item save by string id; a **placed TNT block persists in the block diff** like any block, and a save written mid-fuse reloads with that TNT as an inert, un-lit block (and no creeper). There is no worldgen change — creepers are spawned and TNT is crafted — so neither the `version` nor `WORLDGEN_VERSION` moved. Blast-destroyed blocks are ordinary block-diff edits.
67	- **v5** (unchanged for cow/pig & coal) — the cow and pig mobs (and their meat/leather drops) add no persisted state; mobs are transient and the new foods save by string id. Coal ore, coal, and charcoal are likewise additive (the ore persists in the block diff, the items by string id), so the save _schema_ stays at version 5. But the new coal worldgen changes the deterministic terrain baseline, so **`WORLDGEN_VERSION` is bumped `7` → `8`**: a world whose recorded version differs discards its stale block-diffs and reboots from its seed. Coal runs on its own PRNG (`placeCoal`), so only underground coal cells differ from a v7 world — the surface, existing ores, trees, and structures are byte-identical (the meshing and structural-probe tests stay green; only the byte hashes were re-rolled).
68	- **v5** (unchanged for caves & lighting) — the lighting system adds no persisted state (light is a derived cache, recomputed at load), and lava is worldgen, not a saved field. So the save _schema_ stays at version 5. But the deep-cave lava changes the deterministic terrain baseline, so **`SAVE_KEY` is bumped `minecraft_save_v6` → `minecraft_save_v7`**: old block-diffs were computed against the lava-free world and must never be applied to the new one. Pre-lava saves are discarded in practice. Torches are additive items/blocks, persisted by string id / in the block diff like any other placed block.
69	- **v5** (unchanged for ranged combat & the endgame boss) — bows, arrows, the Cursed Totem, the Dragon Heart, and the Dragon Sword are **additive items**, persisted by string id in the existing inventory/container slots, so no schema change was needed. **Arrows in flight, the boss, its minions, and the `victory` flag are all transient** (never serialized — like mobs), and there is no worldgen change (the boss is summoned, not generated), so neither the `version` nor `SAVE_KEY` moved.
70	- **v5** — adds optional `lootedChests` (opened/broken dungeon loot chests). `migrateSaveV4toV5` is a pure version bump (absent → no dungeon chests yet looted). Unlike v3/v4, **`SAVE_KEY` is bumped to `minecraft_save_v6`** here — not because of the save _shape_ (the field is additive) but because the dungeon worldgen changed the deterministic terrain baseline, so old block-diffs would index against the wrong world. Pre-dungeon saves are therefore discarded in practice; the migration keeps the version chain complete regardless. `readSave` chains v1 → v2 → v3 → v4 → v5 → v6 → v7 → v8 → v9 → v10 → v11 → v12 → v13 → v14 → v15 → v16.
71	- **v4** — adds optional `blockEntities` (chest contents). `migrateSaveV3toV4` is a pure version bump (absent → restores as no containers), so **`SAVE_KEY` was unchanged** at the time (player-placed chests only; worldgen and the index formula were untouched) and v1/v2/v3 saves load fine.
72	- **v3** — adds optional `dayClock`, `hearts`, `hunger`, and `spawnPoint`. `migrateSaveV2toV3` is a pure version bump (the new fields stay absent and restore as engine defaults), so **`SAVE_KEY` is unchanged** and v1/v2 saves load fine.
73	- **v2** — same fields as v1, reinterpreted for the 36-slot inventory and 9-slot hotbar.
74	- **v1** — 40 slots, 10-slot hotbar. Still accepted: `readSave` runs `migrateSaveV1toV2`, which packs non-empty slots in order, merges stackable items into earlier stacks, clamps `selectedSlot` to 0–8, and drops items that overflow the smaller inventory.
75	- Unknown future versions are rejected (treated as no save).
76	
77	## Profiles & worlds
78	
79	Saves are organized two levels deep — a **profile** owns a list of **worlds**, and each world holds one `SaveData` blob. The two small manifests stay in localStorage (they are tiny and read synchronously during render) while the heavy blobs live in IndexedDB. Both manifests are versioned `{ version: 1, ... }` envelopes and their readers are **total** (malformed entries are dropped, never thrown):
80	
81	- **`minecraft_profiles_v1`** (`lib/game/profiles.ts`, localStorage) — the profile list plus `activeProfileId`. A profile is `{ id, name, skinId, createdAt }`: player identity only (name + skin). The skin moved here from the old global `minecraft_skin_v1` key; a dangling `activeProfileId` is repaired on read.
82	- **`minecraft_worlds_v1`** (`lib/game/worlds.ts`, localStorage) — the world index. Each `WorldMeta` is `{ id, profileId, name, seed, worldType, worldgenVersion, createdAt, lastPlayedAt }`; `profileId` is the 1:N owner link and `lastPlayedAt` drives the most-recent-first ordering. The `seed` is resolved once at creation (blank → random, numeric text → clamped int, other text → stable FNV hash via `resolveSeed`); `worldType` is the chosen generation preset (sanitized to `"default"` on read for unknown/legacy entries). Both are the source of truth for regeneration and are also written into the per-world `SaveData` blob.
83	- **`monecraft`/`worldSaves` (IndexedDB)** — one `SaveData` blob per world (the schema above), keyed by world id and read/written through `lib/game/saveStore.ts`. Legacy blobs under the localStorage `minecraft_world_save_<worldId>` keys migrate in transparently (see below).
84	
85	`worldgenVersion` records the `WORLDGEN_VERSION` (`lib/game/config.ts`, currently 11) the world was generated under. This **replaces the old whole-store `SAVE_KEY` bump**: when the worldgen baseline changes, bump `WORLDGEN_VERSION`, and a world whose recorded version differs has its stale block-diffs discarded and reboots from its stored seed — per-world, with no key rename and without touching unaffected worlds.
86	
87	**World types.** A world's `worldType` selects a generation preset (`lib/world/worldTypes.ts`). `generateWorld(world, worldType)` forks on it before any block write (`terrainConfigFor`, `lib/world/generation.ts`), varying only sea level and per-biome surface height; everything else reads `GEN`. The `"default"` branch returns the GEN values verbatim, so default worlds stay **byte-identical** to the pre-feature generator — the existing determinism hashes are unchanged. Each non-default type is its own deterministic save contract with its own SHA-256 baseline in `generation.test.ts`; `worldgenVersion` still guards all types (a deliberate change to any type's config bumps `WORLDGEN_VERSION`, discarding stale worlds of that vintage).
88	
89	The game shell (`components/GameShell.tsx`) drives a profile-select → world-select → play state machine and remembers the tab's active world in `sessionStorage` so a reload resumes it (a fresh tab cold-starts at profile-select). Before a world mounts, its blob is preloaded by the shell's `WorldSaveGate` (IndexedDB reads are async; the engine boot in the mount callback stays synchronous) and handed down as a prop. Deleting a profile cascades its worlds and their save blobs (`deleteWorldsForProfile`). At mount the shell also requests `navigator.storage.persist()` — eviction protection — but only when at least one world exists, so a first-time visitor never sees Firefox's permission prompt.
90	
91	### Legacy migration
92	
93	`migrateLegacySave` (`lib/game/legacyMigration.ts`) runs once on first boot, gated on the **absence** of `minecraft_profiles_v1` (its presence is the already-migrated flag, which survives a rollback that re-creates the legacy key). When a legacy `minecraft_save_v7` exists it creates a default "Player" profile (carrying the old global skin) and **copies** the save into one "My World" blob, then removes the legacy key — the copy precedes the delete so a mid-migration failure can never lose the original. A brand-new player with **no** legacy save gets nothing here; the menu opens straight into the create-profile form (`ProfileSelect` renders it whenever there are zero profiles), so their first act is naming and skinning a profile.
94	
95	**localStorage → IndexedDB migration** follows the same copy-then-delete rule per world key: the shell mount sweeps every `minecraft_world_save_*` localStorage key (`worldSaves.migrateAll` — a prefix scan, so manifest-less `cloud:<id>` blobs and orphans are covered) and the store also migrates lazily on first read of a key. The localStorage original is removed only after the IndexedDB put durably commits; a failed copy leaves it authoritative (reads fall back to it), a corrupt blob is left in place, and the sweep is idempotent with no flag — an empty prefix scan is the terminal state.
96	
97	## Autosave
98	
99	Every 15s via `setInterval` (queued latest-wins write; the "Saved" toast fires on durable commit), plus an **unload flush** on `beforeunload`, `visibilitychange → hidden`, and `pagehide`. The flush starts the put synchronously on the warm connection and commits it explicitly (`IDBTransaction.commit()`); without the explicit commit, auto-commit waits for request callbacks a document mid-teardown never runs and the browser aborts the transaction. All three triggers matter: `beforeunload` fires before the navigation commits, so its transaction has the most teardown headroom (measured in headless Chromium, the later two alone lose the commit race on a large fraction of reloads — keeping `beforeunload` costs back/forward-cache eligibility in Firefox/Safari, a price worth paying for save durability), while `visibilitychange`/`pagehide` cover mobile app-switch and close, where `beforeunload` never fired reliably. "Save & Quit to Worlds" also persists before leaving, because the interval is cleared on unmount and no unload event fires on an in-app world switch; an immediate re-open reads through the store's write queue, so it can never see the pre-save state.
100	
101	## Compatibility rules
102	
103	- Saves store **diffs against generated terrain**, so changing world generation or the voxel index formula (`x + z*sizeX + y*sizeX*sizeZ`) silently corrupts existing saves — bump `WORLDGEN_VERSION` when you do, and each world discards its stale diffs (rebooting from its seed) on the mismatch.
104	- Worldgen output is pinned by SHA-256 characterization tests in `lib/world/generation.test.ts`; they fail on any byte-level change. See [testing.md](testing.md) for the re-baseline policy. Caveat: the noise functions use `Math.sin`, whose exact results are engine-defined — the tests prove refactor purity on the pinned Bun version, not cross-browser save portability.
105	- Changing the save shape requires bumping the `version` field and handling (or discarding) old data. Round-trip tests live in `lib/game/save.test.ts` and `lib/game/engine/GameEngine.test.ts`.
106	- Durable gear restores at a maximum count of one per slot. The v1→v2 migration
107	  splits legacy stacked gear into separate slots until inventory capacity is
108	  exhausted; current malformed stacks are clamped to one.
109	- Note save-format/worldgen impact in PRs.
110

# Save format & compatibility

## Schema

`SaveData` (version 17) in `lib/game/types.ts`. Since v17 the per-player
fields below (inventory, equipped armor, selected slot, position,
hearts/hunger, effects, xp, stats, advancements, spawn point, game mode,
gameOver) live inside `players: SavedPlayer[]` — a single `"local"` entry in
single-player — while the world-level fields stay top-level (see the v17
entry under Version history). The field-by-field contracts are unchanged:

- world `seed`
- `worldType` (optional) — the generation preset (`"default"` | `"flat"` | `"amplified"` | `"islands"`); absent ⇒ `"default"`. Like `seed`, it is fixed for the world's life and the world must always regenerate with it, since the block-diffs were recorded against that terrain
- `gameMode` (optional) — the player's game mode (`"survival"` | `"creative"` | `"adventure"` | `"spectator"`); absent ⇒ `"survival"`. Unlike `worldType`, this is **switchable in-game** (pause menu), so the saved value is the _current_ mode, not the one chosen at creation. Restored by `restoreGameMode` (`lib/game/save.ts`); `isFlying` is session-only and never serialized
- `difficulty` (optional) — the player's difficulty (`"peaceful"` | `"easy"` | `"normal"` | `"hard"`); absent ⇒ `"normal"`. An axis orthogonal to `gameMode`, and likewise **switchable in-game** (pause menu), so the saved value is the _current_ difficulty. Restored by `restoreDifficulty` (`lib/game/save.ts`); the per-level multipliers live in `lib/game/difficulties.ts`, the starvation accumulator (`starvationTimer`) is session-only
- `hardcore` (optional) — the Hardcore flag (`boolean`); absent ⇒ `false`. **Immutable** (unlike `gameMode`/`difficulty`): a hardcore world is forced to Survival + Hard and the engine locks both switchers. Restored by `restoreHardcore`
- `gameOver` (optional) — the permadeath flag (`boolean`); absent ⇒ `false`. Set once a hardcore run has ended in death; a reloaded `gameOver` world boots into the spectator "dead world" state (never playable). Restored by `restoreGameOver`. (The transient `isDead`/`respawnTimer` stay session-only — hardcore death is captured by this flag instead.)
- a block **diff** list — `changes: [blockIndex, blockId][]`; edits that revert to the generated baseline are pruned (player-placed crops, beds, furnaces, chests, and both halves/states of doors ride this list — they are ordinary block edits)
- inventory slots with durability, **enchantments, and a custom name** (36 slots; the first 9 are the hotbar). Each `SavedSlot` is `{ id, count, durability?, enchantments?, customName? }`; `enchantments` (`{ id, level }[]`) and `customName` (the anvil rename) ride durable gear only and are validated on load (`restoreSlot` — known enchant ids via `Object.hasOwn`, levels clamped to `1..ENCHANT_MAX_LEVEL`; `customName` trimmed and capped to `CUSTOM_NAME_MAX_LEN`, blanks dropped). The same path serializes chest contents
- `xp` (optional) — banked experience points (`XP_PER_LEVEL` points = one level). Earned from kills/ore/fishing, spent at the enchanting table. Restored by `restoreXp` (finite, ≥ 0). Unlike effects, XP is a currency and is **kept across death**
- equipped armor — the worn pieces themselves (one per slot, dedicated storage), persisted as per-slot `SavedSlot` via `serializeEquippedArmor`/`restoreEquippedArmor` (so worn durability/enchantments/customName survive). A worn piece lives **only** here, not in the 36 inventory slots
- selected hotbar slot (0–8)
- player position — validated on load by `restorePlayerPosition` (`lib/game/save.ts`): coords keep their fractional part (the player isn't grid-aligned) but a missing or non-finite (NaN/Infinity) position is rejected, leaving the fresh spawn in place so a corrupt blob can't load a broken world or slip past the `position.y < 2` unstuck net
- `dayClock`, `hearts`, `hunger` (all optional) — time of day and player stats, so sleeping through the night and a hurt/hungry player survive a reload
- `spawnPoint` (optional, `{x,y,z}` or null) — the bed respawn point; respawn falls back to a random land point when it is null or the block there is no longer a bed
- `blockEntities` (optional) — chest contents as `{ index, slots }[]`, keyed by the block's voxel index (the same index space as `changes`). Only **non-empty** chests are stored; an empty one carries no data and is recreated empty when opened. On load each entry is kept only if that index still holds a Chest block. This is the first per-block metadata in the format — `lib/game/save.ts` (`serializeContainers` / `readContainers`) handles it
- `effects` (optional) — active status effects as `{ id, remaining }[]` (remaining in seconds). Drink-granted buffs (Speed/Strength/Regeneration/Fire Resistance/Water Breathing) and the rotten-flesh Poison hazard live in `state.effects` (a Map) and persist here, but are **cleared on death**, so a saved-then-reloaded world resumes whatever was active at save time. On load, `restoreEffects` (`lib/game/save.ts`) drops unknown ids and non-positive/garbage durations
- `lootedChests` (optional) — voxel indices of **worldgen** loot chests (dungeon, shipwreck, or buried treasure) the player has already opened or broken. Worldgen chests' contents are **not** in `changes`/`blockEntities` until accessed; the engine fills them lazily on first access (loot seeded from `world.seed ^ index`, mixed with a per-family constant, from the family's own table) and records the index here. Because an emptied chest drops out of `blockEntities`, this set — not the chest's emptiness — is what prevents a re-roll on reload. The session-only sets of _which_ indices belong to each family are not stored; they are re-derived from the seed each load via `collectDungeonSites` / `collectShipwreckSites` / `collectTreasureSites` (`lib/world/generation.ts`). The field kept its name when shipwrecks/buried treasure generalized it (state-side it is `lootedWorldgenChests`), so pre-aquatic saves read unchanged. Handled by `serializeLootedChests` / `readLootedChests` in `lib/game/save.ts`
- `stats` (optional) — gameplay **statistics** as `{ id, value }[]` (blocks mined, mobs killed, items crafted/enchanted, potions drunk, fish caught, distance travelled, time played, …). Counters live in `state.stats` (a `Map<string, number>`) and are folded in at the engine's single emit chokepoint (`recordEvent`/`recordTick`, `lib/game/engine/systems/advancements.ts`). Like `xp` and **unlike `effects`**, they are a long-term record and are **kept across death**. Only positive values are written; `restoreStats` (`lib/game/save.ts`) drops non-string ids and negative/garbage values. The id set is open (per-recipe `crafted_<id>` and per-block `*_mined` counters), so there's no allow-list
- `advancements` (optional) — the unlocked **advancement** ids as `string[]`. Unlock is uniform — `state.stats.get(stat) >= threshold` for each declarative entry in `ADVANCEMENTS` (`lib/game/engine/systems/advancements.ts`) — and ids accumulate in `state.advancements` (a `Set`). Also **kept across death**; `restoreAdvancements` (`lib/game/save.ts`) keeps non-empty strings only, de-duplicated. Unknown persisted ids (e.g. a renamed entry) are harmless: they round-trip but never re-unlock, since `evaluateAdvancements` only iterates the registry
- `mobs` (optional) — persisted mobs as `SavedMob[]` (`{ kind, x, y, z, hp, faction, owner?, sitting?, ageTimer?, profession? }`). The fungible wild/hostile population is re-seeded each boot by `spawnInitialMobs`, so only mobs matching `isPersistentMob` are written: **tamed pets** (`owner` set) and **village residents** (`faction === "villager"`). `serializeMobs`/`restoreMobs` (`lib/game/save.ts`) round-trip and validate — dropping unknown kinds, non-finite coords, non-positive hp, and anything that isn't a valid persistent shape (an owned ally pet, or an owner-less villager); a resident's `profession` (v15) is validated against the known set. The engine rebuilds each live `MobState` **before** `spawnInitialMobs`, re-grounding `y` onto the current surface (the world may have changed), assigning fresh ids (the renderer reconciles by id from a cold boot), and clamping hp + re-arming a pet's detect range. Like `xp`/`stats` and **unlike `effects`**, persisted mobs are kept across death
- `vehicles` (optional) — placed water vehicles as `SavedVehicle[]` (`{ kind, x, y, z, yaw }`, where `kind` is `"raft"` or `"ship"`). The live rider link (`mountedVehicleId` / `VehicleState.rider`) is session-only and never serialized; reloads restore only the placed entities. `serializeVehicles`/`restoreVehicles` (`lib/game/save.ts`) round-trip and validate — dropping unknown kinds and non-finite poses — and the engine only keeps restored vehicles that still sit on valid water support

Each world's `SaveData` is stored in **IndexedDB** — database `monecraft`, object store `worldSaves`, keyed by world id (including the synthetic `cloud:<id>` ids) — as a structured clone of the object, not a JSON string, so it lives off localStorage's ~5–10 MB origin quota. The async store is `lib/game/saveStore.ts` (`worldSaves.read/write/remove/flushWrite`) over the minimal wrapper in `lib/game/idbKv.ts`; writes are queued per world with latest-wins coalescing, reads are read-your-writes (a remount can never see a stale blob), and `write()` resolves only when the transaction has durably committed. Validation and the migration chain live in `lib/game/save.ts` — every read (either container) flows through `parseSave`; the sync `readSave`/`writeSave` (injectable `Storage`) remain for the legacy localStorage keys `minecraft_world_save_<worldId>` (`worldSaveKey` in `lib/game/worlds.ts`), which are now only a migration source, the store's fallback when IndexedDB is unavailable (some private modes — old behavior, quota risk included), and the server's save path (`server/persistence.ts`). `GameEngine.serialize()` produces the save from live state, and `lib/game/engine/blockChanges.ts` maintains the block diff. (The legacy single-world key `SAVE_KEY` = `minecraft_save_v7` is read only once, by the migration described under [Profiles & worlds](#profiles--worlds).)

Audio volume preferences live under a **separate**, global key (`minecraft_audio_v1`, `lib/game/audio/settings.ts`), shared across all profiles and not part of any world save or its versioning.

**Per-voxel light is never serialized.** It is a derived cache (`world.light`), recomputed from the blocks at load by `computeFullLight` and patched locally on every edit (`lib/world/lighting.ts`); the bake reads only `world.blocks`, so the save needs no lighting field.

Continuous-water exposure, lava burn, and the oxygen/drowning meter all live only
in transient `GameTimers`/state. Saving, reloading, or respawning resets them
(breath restores to full). The status-effect **accumulators** (`effectRegenTimer`,
`effectPoisonTimer`) are likewise transient — but the effects **themselves**
(`state.effects`) persist via the `effects` field above and survive a reload.

### Version history

- **v17** (the players array — multiplayer groundwork) — every per-player field moves off the top level into `players: SavedPlayer[]`; world-level fields (seed, worldType, difficulty, hardcore, changes, blockEntities, lootedChests, mobs, vehicles, dayClock, villagesSeeded) stay put. `SavedPlayer` keeps the old field names (one rename: the top-level `player` position becomes `position`) so the per-field validators are shared between migration and live restores. `migrateSaveV16toV17` is a pure field move wrapping a flat single-player save as `[{ id: "local", … }]`, and rewrites pet owners from the legacy literal `"player"` to `"local"` — `SavedMob.owner` is a real player id from here on. A single-player world always saves one `"local"` entry; a multiplayer server holds one entry per known account and restores a joining player's slice through the same `restorePlayerFields` mirror that `serialize()` writes. Hardcore's `gameOver` is per-player (`restoreGameOver(save, savedPlayer)` requires the world's `hardcore` flag as before).
- **Unreleased (no save bump; `WORLDGEN_VERSION` 10→11)** — **portable worldgen noise**. Every seed-determined noise call (terrain waves, biome fields, cave-walk trig, the underground speckle hash) moved from `Math.sin` — whose results are engine-defined, so the same seed could generate different terrain on different JS engines — to the bit-portable implementations in `lib/world/noise.ts`. Same formulas, near-identical terrain (all structural probes unchanged), but exact bytes shift: old worlds discard stale block-diffs and reboot from their seed, and all worldgen digests were re-baselined into `lib/world/generationBaselines.ts` per docs/testing.md. The save **schema stays v16** — no field changes. This makes seed + block-diff sync portable between a browser and a Bun multiplayer server, and is proven in CI by `e2e/determinism.e2e.ts` (Chromium digest ≡ Bun baseline). Weather windows and the daylight curve moved to the same portable primitives (both transient/derived — no save impact).
- **0.12.0 (no save bump; `WORLDGEN_VERSION` 9→10)** — the **aquatic update**. Kelp/coral (`BlockId`s **appended**: 55–57), sunken **shipwrecks**, and **buried treasure** all write generated blocks, so the worldgen baseline bumps 9→10 (old worlds discard stale block-diffs and reboot from their seed; the worldgen/world-type/meshing digests were re-baselined per docs/testing.md). The save **schema stays v16**: cod/salmon are fungible wild mobs (never persisted; `restoreMobs` in older builds drops unknown kinds), kelp growth/harvest rides the block diff, the `treasure_map`/`dried_kelp`/coral items are additive string ids with **no instance state** (the map's compass target is derived from the seed at runtime), and shipwreck/buried chests reuse the persisted `lootedChests` index set unchanged (see above — the fill family is re-derived, not stored).
- **v16** (water vehicles) — adds optional top-level `vehicles` (`SavedVehicle[]`) for placed **rafts** and **ships**. `migrateSaveV15toV16` is a pure version bump (absent ⇒ no placed vehicles). Vehicle items are additive string ids; placed vehicles are entities, not voxel blocks, so there is **no `BlockId` or worldgen change** (`WORLDGEN_VERSION` stays 9). The rider/mount state is transient and reloads with the player unmounted.
- **v15** (villager professions — Living World, PR 2) — adds an optional `profession` (`"farmer" | "blacksmith" | "librarian" | "cleric"`) on a villager resident's `SavedMob`. `migrateSaveV14toV15` is a pure version bump (absent ⇒ the engine assigns one round-robin at boot). Validated against the known professions on load. **Generated villages** in the same release bump **`WORLDGEN_VERSION` 8→9** (villages add structures, so old block-diffs are stale and discarded — the worldgen/world-type/meshing digests were re-baselined per docs/testing.md); village residents persist via the existing v14 `mobs` field, and **raids** are transient (`state.raid` + raiders aren't serialized, like the boss), so neither needs further save schema beyond the additive `profession` and the by-id Ominous Horn item.
- **v14** (persisted mobs — Living World, PR 1) — adds an optional top-level `mobs` (`SavedMob[]`). `migrateSaveV13toV14` is a pure version bump (absent ⇒ no persisted mobs; the world re-seeds its wildlife as before). This is the first mob persistence in the format: `isPersistentMob` keeps only **tamed pets** here (PR-B adds village residents), since the fungible population is re-created each boot. Restored before `spawnInitialMobs`, with `y` re-grounded onto the current surface and fresh ids assigned. The new `faction`/`owner`/`sitting`/`targetId`/`retargetTimer` mob fields are session-side; only the durable ones land in `SavedMob`. The wolf and cat are additive `MobKind`s with no `BlockId`/item changes, so **`WORLDGEN_VERSION` stays at 8** and `SAVE_KEY` is unchanged.
- **v13** (advancements & statistics) — adds optional top-level `stats` (`{ id, value }[]`) and `advancements` (`string[]`). `migrateSaveV12toV13` is a pure version bump (both absent ⇒ no stats, no advancements yet earned). Both are progression meta folded in at the engine's single emit chokepoint and, like `xp` and **unlike `effects`**, are **kept across death** (`clearEffects` never touches them). `serializeStats`/`restoreStats` and `restoreAdvancements` (`lib/game/save.ts`) round-trip and validate them. No new `BlockId`, no new item, and no worldgen change — advancement icons reuse existing item/block sprites — so **`WORLDGEN_VERSION` stays at 8** and `SAVE_KEY` is unchanged.
- **Unreleased (no save bump)** — new enchantments (**Power**, **Punch**, **Knockback**, **Looting**, **Fortune**, **Feather Falling**) ride the existing per-slot `enchantments` field, and new status effects (**Haste**, **Resistance**, **Jump Boost**) ride the existing top-level `effects` field. Their ids are added to the save validators' known-id sets (`VALID_ENCHANT_IDS` / `VALID_EFFECT_IDS`, both compile-enforced `Record<…, true>`). No new field, no new `BlockId`, no worldgen change — the save schema stays **v12** and **`WORLDGEN_VERSION` stays at 8** (the same additive-id pattern as Mending). Older builds silently drop unknown ids on load.
- **v12** (dedicated armor storage) — fixes a bug where equipped armor stayed in the inventory and occupied a hotbar/storage slot. `equippedArmor` is no longer a by-id reference into `inventorySlots` but the worn pieces themselves, persisted per slot as `SavedSlot` (via `serializeEquippedArmor`/`restoreEquippedArmor`, reusing the shared `restoreSlot` validation). `migrateSaveV11toV12` moves each legacy by-id equip out of `inventorySlots` into the armor record (preserving durability/enchantments/customName; equips whose item isn't found or isn't valid armor are dropped; a legacy `inventoryCounts`-only save just drops the equip map and keeps the items). No worldgen change — **`WORLDGEN_VERSION` stays at 8** and `SAVE_KEY` is unchanged.
- **v11** (anvil rename & Mending) — adds an optional `customName` on each `SavedSlot` (the anvil rename). `migrateSaveV10toV11` is a pure version bump (absent ⇒ no custom name). `customName` rides the existing `inventorySlotsSnapshot`/`restoreSlot` path (shared by inventory and chests), is restored on durable gear only, and is trimmed + capped to `CUSTOM_NAME_MAX_LEN` with blanks dropped. The **Mending** enchantment adds no new field — it rides the existing per-slot `enchantments` (and its `mending` id is added to the save validator's known-id set). The **Anvil** and **Grindstone** items save by string id and their `BlockId`s are **appended** so saved block ids never shift. No worldgen change — both are craft-only — so **`WORLDGEN_VERSION` stays at 8**.
- **v10** (Hardcore) — adds optional top-level `hardcore` and `gameOver` booleans. `migrateSaveV9toV10` is a pure version bump (both absent ⇒ a normal, non-hardcore world, via `restoreHardcore`/`restoreGameOver`). `hardcore` is immutable (forces Survival + Hard, locks both switchers); `gameOver` is the persisted permadeath flag, so a dead hardcore world reloads into its spectator state rather than respawning (the transient `isDead`/`respawnTimer` remain session-only). No worldgen change — so **`WORLDGEN_VERSION` stays at 8**.
- **v9** (difficulty) — adds an optional top-level `difficulty` (`"peaceful"` | `"easy"` | `"normal"` | `"hard"`). `migrateSaveV8toV9` is a pure version bump (absent ⇒ `"normal"`, via `restoreDifficulty`). Difficulty is an axis orthogonal to `gameMode`, switchable in-game, so the _current_ level is what's stored; the per-level multipliers live in `lib/game/difficulties.ts` and the `starvationTimer` accumulator is session-only. No worldgen change — difficulty touches no generation — so **`WORLDGEN_VERSION` stays at 8**.
- **v8** (game modes) — adds an optional top-level `gameMode` (`"survival"` | `"creative"` | `"adventure"` | `"spectator"`). `migrateSaveV7toV8` is a pure version bump (absent ⇒ `"survival"`, via `restoreGameMode`). The mode is switchable in-game, so the _current_ mode is what's stored; the transient `isFlying` is never serialized. No worldgen change — modes touch no generation — so **`WORLDGEN_VERSION` stays at 8**.
- **v7** (XP & enchanting) — adds optional top-level `xp` and an optional `enchantments` array on each `SavedSlot`. `migrateSaveV6toV7` is a pure version bump (absent → xp 0, no enchantments). XP persists and is **kept across death** (it's a currency, not a status effect); enchantments ride the existing `inventorySlotsSnapshot`/`restoreSlot` path (shared by inventory and chests) and are validated on load. The **Enchanting Table** item saves by string id and the `EnchantingTable` `BlockId` is **appended** (id 52) so saved block ids never shift. No worldgen change — **`WORLDGEN_VERSION` stays at 8**.
- **v6** (status effects, brewing & potions) — adds optional `effects` (`{ id, remaining }[]`). `migrateSaveV5toV6` is a pure version bump (absent → no active effects), so pre-effect saves load clean. Effects persist but are cleared on death; `serializeEffects`/`restoreEffects` (`lib/game/save.ts`) round-trip and validate them. Potions, glass bottles, and the **Brewing Stand** item save by string id; the `BrewingStand` `BlockId` is **appended at the end** of the enum (id 51) so existing saved block ids never shift, and a placed stand persists in the block diff like any block. No worldgen change — the new effects/recipes touch no generation — so **`WORLDGEN_VERSION` stays at 8** and the determinism hashes are untouched.
- **v5** (unchanged for fishing) — the active cast is the session-only `state.fishing` field (a transient bobber, like in-flight arrows and thrown spears); it is never serialized and is cleared on respawn. The fishing rod and raw/cooked fish are additive items saved by string id, and a catch is an ordinary inventory change. No worldgen change, so neither the `version` nor `WORLDGEN_VERSION` moved.
- **v5** (unchanged for the living world — saplings, bone meal & grass spread) — every effect is an ordinary block edit that rides the `changes` diff: a planted sapling, a grown tree's wood and leaves, and re-grassed dirt all persist with no new fields, and bone meal is an additive item saved by string id. The `Sapling` `BlockId` is **appended at the end** of the enum (id 50) so existing saved block ids never shift. Crucially, the runtime tree grower (`systems/treeGrowth.ts`) shares **no** code with worldgen's hash-pinned `placeTrees`, so the generated terrain is byte-identical and **neither the `version` nor `WORLDGEN_VERSION` moved**.
- **v5** (unchanged for villagers & trading) — the villager mob is transient like every mob, and trading needs no persisted state: a trade is a station-gated recipe (`station: "villager"`) run through the existing `craft` command, the open trade station (`craftingStation`) is session-only, and there are no per-trade use caps to store. **Emerald** and any traded goods save by string id in the existing inventory slots. No worldgen change (villagers spawn into the passive population; there are no village structures), so neither the `version` nor `WORLDGEN_VERSION` moved.
- **v5** (unchanged for creepers & TNT) — the creeper mob, gunpowder, and the explosion system add no persisted state: mobs are transient, **a creeper's lit fuse and a primed TNT block's countdown are session-only** (`MobState.fuseTimer` and `state.primedTnt` are never serialized — like the boss and in-flight arrows). Gunpowder and the TNT item save by string id; a **placed TNT block persists in the block diff** like any block, and a save written mid-fuse reloads with that TNT as an inert, un-lit block (and no creeper). There is no worldgen change — creepers are spawned and TNT is crafted — so neither the `version` nor `WORLDGEN_VERSION` moved. Blast-destroyed blocks are ordinary block-diff edits.
- **v5** (unchanged for cow/pig & coal) — the cow and pig mobs (and their meat/leather drops) add no persisted state; mobs are transient and the new foods save by string id. Coal ore, coal, and charcoal are likewise additive (the ore persists in the block diff, the items by string id), so the save _schema_ stays at version 5. But the new coal worldgen changes the deterministic terrain baseline, so **`WORLDGEN_VERSION` is bumped `7` → `8`**: a world whose recorded version differs discards its stale block-diffs and reboots from its seed. Coal runs on its own PRNG (`placeCoal`), so only underground coal cells differ from a v7 world — the surface, existing ores, trees, and structures are byte-identical (the meshing and structural-probe tests stay green; only the byte hashes were re-rolled).
- **v5** (unchanged for caves & lighting) — the lighting system adds no persisted state (light is a derived cache, recomputed at load), and lava is worldgen, not a saved field. So the save _schema_ stays at version 5. But the deep-cave lava changes the deterministic terrain baseline, so **`SAVE_KEY` is bumped `minecraft_save_v6` → `minecraft_save_v7`**: old block-diffs were computed against the lava-free world and must never be applied to the new one. Pre-lava saves are discarded in practice. Torches are additive items/blocks, persisted by string id / in the block diff like any other placed block.
- **v5** (unchanged for ranged combat & the endgame boss) — bows, arrows, the Cursed Totem, the Dragon Heart, and the Dragon Sword are **additive items**, persisted by string id in the existing inventory/container slots, so no schema change was needed. **Arrows in flight, the boss, its minions, and the `victory` flag are all transient** (never serialized — like mobs), and there is no worldgen change (the boss is summoned, not generated), so neither the `version` nor `SAVE_KEY` moved.
- **v5** — adds optional `lootedChests` (opened/broken dungeon loot chests). `migrateSaveV4toV5` is a pure version bump (absent → no dungeon chests yet looted). Unlike v3/v4, **`SAVE_KEY` is bumped to `minecraft_save_v6`** here — not because of the save _shape_ (the field is additive) but because the dungeon worldgen changed the deterministic terrain baseline, so old block-diffs would index against the wrong world. Pre-dungeon saves are therefore discarded in practice; the migration keeps the version chain complete regardless. `readSave` chains v1 → v2 → v3 → v4 → v5 → v6 → v7 → v8 → v9 → v10 → v11 → v12 → v13 → v14 → v15 → v16.
- **v4** — adds optional `blockEntities` (chest contents). `migrateSaveV3toV4` is a pure version bump (absent → restores as no containers), so **`SAVE_KEY` was unchanged** at the time (player-placed chests only; worldgen and the index formula were untouched) and v1/v2/v3 saves load fine.
- **v3** — adds optional `dayClock`, `hearts`, `hunger`, and `spawnPoint`. `migrateSaveV2toV3` is a pure version bump (the new fields stay absent and restore as engine defaults), so **`SAVE_KEY` is unchanged** and v1/v2 saves load fine.
- **v2** — same fields as v1, reinterpreted for the 36-slot inventory and 9-slot hotbar.
- **v1** — 40 slots, 10-slot hotbar. Still accepted: `readSave` runs `migrateSaveV1toV2`, which packs non-empty slots in order, merges stackable items into earlier stacks, clamps `selectedSlot` to 0–8, and drops items that overflow the smaller inventory.
- Unknown future versions are rejected (treated as no save).

## Profiles & worlds

Saves are organized two levels deep — a **profile** owns a list of **worlds**, and each world holds one `SaveData` blob. The two small manifests stay in localStorage (they are tiny and read synchronously during render) while the heavy blobs live in IndexedDB. Both manifests are versioned `{ version: 1, ... }` envelopes and their readers are **total** (malformed entries are dropped, never thrown):

- **`minecraft_profiles_v1`** (`lib/game/profiles.ts`, localStorage) — the profile list plus `activeProfileId`. A profile is `{ id, name, skinId, createdAt }`: player identity only (name + skin). The skin moved here from the old global `minecraft_skin_v1` key; a dangling `activeProfileId` is repaired on read.
- **`minecraft_worlds_v1`** (`lib/game/worlds.ts`, localStorage) — the world index. Each `WorldMeta` is `{ id, profileId, name, seed, worldType, worldgenVersion, createdAt, lastPlayedAt }`; `profileId` is the 1:N owner link and `lastPlayedAt` drives the most-recent-first ordering. The `seed` is resolved once at creation (blank → random, numeric text → clamped int, other text → stable FNV hash via `resolveSeed`); `worldType` is the chosen generation preset (sanitized to `"default"` on read for unknown/legacy entries). Both are the source of truth for regeneration and are also written into the per-world `SaveData` blob.
- **`monecraft`/`worldSaves` (IndexedDB)** — one `SaveData` blob per world (the schema above), keyed by world id and read/written through `lib/game/saveStore.ts`. Legacy blobs under the localStorage `minecraft_world_save_<worldId>` keys migrate in transparently (see below).

`worldgenVersion` records the `WORLDGEN_VERSION` (`lib/game/config.ts`, currently 11) the world was generated under. This **replaces the old whole-store `SAVE_KEY` bump**: when the worldgen baseline changes, bump `WORLDGEN_VERSION`, and a world whose recorded version differs has its stale block-diffs discarded and reboots from its stored seed — per-world, with no key rename and without touching unaffected worlds.

**World types.** A world's `worldType` selects a generation preset (`lib/world/worldTypes.ts`). `generateWorld(world, worldType)` forks on it before any block write (`terrainConfigFor`, `lib/world/generation.ts`), varying only sea level and per-biome surface height; everything else reads `GEN`. The `"default"` branch returns the GEN values verbatim, so default worlds stay **byte-identical** to the pre-feature generator — the existing determinism hashes are unchanged. Each non-default type is its own deterministic save contract with its own SHA-256 baseline in `generation.test.ts`; `worldgenVersion` still guards all types (a deliberate change to any type's config bumps `WORLDGEN_VERSION`, discarding stale worlds of that vintage).

The game shell (`components/GameShell.tsx`) drives a profile-select → world-select → play state machine and remembers the tab's active world in `sessionStorage` so a reload resumes it (a fresh tab cold-starts at profile-select). Before a world mounts, its blob is preloaded by the shell's `WorldSaveGate` (IndexedDB reads are async; the engine boot in the mount callback stays synchronous) and handed down as a prop. Deleting a profile cascades its worlds and their save blobs (`deleteWorldsForProfile`). At mount the shell also requests `navigator.storage.persist()` — eviction protection — but only when at least one world exists, so a first-time visitor never sees Firefox's permission prompt.

### Legacy migration

`migrateLegacySave` (`lib/game/legacyMigration.ts`) runs once on first boot, gated on the **absence** of `minecraft_profiles_v1` (its presence is the already-migrated flag, which survives a rollback that re-creates the legacy key). When a legacy `minecraft_save_v7` exists it creates a default "Player" profile (carrying the old global skin) and **copies** the save into one "My World" blob, then removes the legacy key — the copy precedes the delete so a mid-migration failure can never lose the original. A brand-new player with **no** legacy save gets nothing here; the menu opens straight into the create-profile form (`ProfileSelect` renders it whenever there are zero profiles), so their first act is naming and skinning a profile.

**localStorage → IndexedDB migration** follows the same copy-then-delete rule per world key: the shell mount sweeps every `minecraft_world_save_*` localStorage key (`worldSaves.migrateAll` — a prefix scan, so manifest-less `cloud:<id>` blobs and orphans are covered) and the store also migrates lazily on first read of a key. The localStorage original is removed only after the IndexedDB put durably commits; a failed copy leaves it authoritative (reads fall back to it), a corrupt blob is left in place, and the sweep is idempotent with no flag — an empty prefix scan is the terminal state.

## Autosave

Every 15s via `setInterval` (queued latest-wins write; the "Saved" toast fires on durable commit), plus an **unload flush** on `beforeunload`, `visibilitychange → hidden`, and `pagehide`. The flush starts the put synchronously on the warm connection and commits it explicitly (`IDBTransaction.commit()`); without the explicit commit, auto-commit waits for request callbacks a document mid-teardown never runs and the browser aborts the transaction. All three triggers matter: `beforeunload` fires before the navigation commits, so its transaction has the most teardown headroom (measured in headless Chromium, the later two alone lose the commit race on a large fraction of reloads — keeping `beforeunload` costs back/forward-cache eligibility in Firefox/Safari, a price worth paying for save durability), while `visibilitychange`/`pagehide` cover mobile app-switch and close, where `beforeunload` never fired reliably. "Save & Quit to Worlds" also persists before leaving, because the interval is cleared on unmount and no unload event fires on an in-app world switch; an immediate re-open reads through the store's write queue, so it can never see the pre-save state.

## Compatibility rules

- Saves store **diffs against generated terrain**, so changing world generation or the voxel index formula (`x + z*sizeX + y*sizeX*sizeZ`) silently corrupts existing saves — bump `WORLDGEN_VERSION` when you do, and each world discards its stale diffs (rebooting from its seed) on the mismatch.
- Worldgen output is pinned by SHA-256 characterization tests in `lib/world/generation.test.ts`; they fail on any byte-level change. See [testing.md](testing.md) for the re-baseline policy. Caveat: the noise functions use `Math.sin`, whose exact results are engine-defined — the tests prove refactor purity on the pinned Bun version, not cross-browser save portability.
- Changing the save shape requires bumping the `version` field and handling (or discarding) old data. Round-trip tests live in `lib/game/save.test.ts` and `lib/game/engine/GameEngine.test.ts`.
- Durable gear restores at a maximum count of one per slot. The v1→v2 migration
  splits legacy stacked gear into separate slots until inventory capacity is
  exhausted; current malformed stacks are clamped to one.
- Note save-format/worldgen impact in PRs.

An engine re-emits sections it does not simulate **verbatim** (`foreignDimensions` / `foreignOverworld` on `GameEngine`) — the server room (always overworld) round-trips a world's nether builds without knowing they exist. ⚠️ **Drift trap:** a field added to `serialize()`'s world half must be added to `DimensionSection` too, or it silently stays overworld-global (pinned by the byte-equality pass-through test in `GameEngine.test.ts`)

Unlock is uniform — `state.stats.get(stat) >= threshold` for each declarative entry in `ADVANCEMENTS` (`lib/game/engine/systems/advancements.ts`) — and ids accumulate in `state.advancements` (a `Set`). Also **kept across death**; `restoreAdvancements` (`lib/game/save.ts`) keeps non-empty strings only, de-duplicated. Unknown persisted ids (e.g. a renamed entry) are harmless: they round-trip but never re-unlock, since `evaluateAdvancements` only iterates the registry

- `mobs` (optional) — persisted mobs as `SavedMob[]` (`{ kind, x, y, z, hp, faction, owner?, sitting?, ageTimer?, profession? }`). The fungible wild/hostile population is re-seeded each boot by `spawnInitialMobs`, so only mobs matching `isPersistentMob` are written: **tamed pets** (`owner` set) and **village residents** (`faction === "villager"`). `serializeMobs`/`restoreMobs` (`lib/game/save.ts`) round-trip and validate — dropping unknown kinds, non-finite coords, non-positive hp, and anything that isn't a valid persistent shape (an owned ally pet, or an owner-less villager); a resident's `profession` (v15) is validated against the known set. The engine rebuilds each live `MobState` **before** `spawnInitialMobs`, re-grounding `y` onto the current surface (the world may have changed), assigning fresh ids (the renderer reconciles by id from a cold boot), and clamping hp + re-arming a pet's detect range. Like `xp`/`stats` and **unlike `effects`**, persisted mobs are kept across death

- `vehicles` (optional) — placed water vehicles as `SavedVehicle[]` (`{ kind, x, y, z, yaw }`, where `kind` is `"raft"` or `"ship"`). The live rider link (`mountedVehicleId` / `VehicleState.rider`) is session-only and never serialized; reloads restore only the placed entities. `serializeVehicles`/`restoreVehicles` (`lib/game/save.ts`) round-trip and validate — dropping unknown kinds and non-finite poses — and the engine only keeps restored vehicles that still sit on valid water support

+- `worldgenVersion` (optional) — the `WORLDGEN_VERSION` stamped by `serialize()`. `applyWorldgenGuard` (`lib/game/save.ts`), run first thing in the `GameEngine` constructor (one seam covering single-player, cloud saves, and the server room), enforces the staleness rule: a **mismatched** stamp discards every dimension's world half (changes, blockEntities, lootedChests, mobs, vehicles, dimensions, villagesSeeded) and the world reboots from its seed with the players kept. An **absent** stamp (anything migrated from ≤ v17) is grandfathered untouched — the guard only ever acts on a stamp it wrote itself

+- `dimensions` (optional) — non-overworld world halves, currently `{ nether?: DimensionSection }`. A `DimensionSection` carries exactly the world-half fields (`changes`, `blockEntities?`, `lootedChests?`, `mobs?`, `vehicles?`) with voxel indices in **that dimension's** coordinate space. `dimensionSectionOf(save, dimension)` maps the overworld to the top level and other dimensions to their section, so restore code is dimension-agnostic. An engine re-emits sections it does not simulate **verbatim** (`foreignDimensions` / `foreignOverworld` on `GameEngine`) — the server room (always overworld) round-trips a world's nether builds without knowing they exist. ⚠️ **Drift trap:** a field added to `serialize()`'s world half must be added to `DimensionSection` too, or it silently stays overworld-global (pinned by the byte-equality pass-through test in `GameEngine.test.ts`)

+- per-player `dimension` (optional) — where that player is (`"overworld"` | `"nether"`); absent ⇒ overworld. Restored by `restorePlayerDimension`; the engine boots into the **local player's** dimension (swap-on-travel: one live dimension per engine)

+- per-player `portalArrival` (optional) — a one-shot arrival anchor written **only** by `serializeForTravel` (never by an ordinary save) and consumed at the next boot: the engine finds or builds the arrival portal there (`ensureArrivalPortal`) before the light bake, so the built portal persists as ordinary diff and the operation is idempotent across a crash

Each world's `SaveData` is stored in **IndexedDB** — database `monecraft`, object store `worldSaves`, keyed by world id (including the synthetic `cloud:<id>` ids) — as a structured clone of the object, not a JSON string, so it lives off localStorage's ~5–10 MB origin quota. The async store is `lib/game/saveStore.ts` (`worldSaves.read/write/remove/flushWrite`) over the minimal wrapper in `lib/game/idbKv.ts`; writes are queued per world with latest-wins coalescing, reads are read-your-writes (a remount can never see a stale blob), and `write()` resolves only when the transaction has durably committed. Validation and the migration chain live in `lib/game/save.ts` — every read (either container) flows through `parseSave`; the sync `readSave`/`writeSave` (injectable `Storage`) remain for the legacy localStorage keys `minecraft_world_save_<worldId>` (`worldSaveKey` in `lib/game/worlds.ts`), which are now only a migration source, the store's fallback when IndexedDB is unavailable (some private modes — old behavior, quota risk included), and the server's save path (`server/persistence.ts`). `GameEngine.serialize()` produces the save from live state, and `lib/game/engine/blockChanges.ts` maintains the block diff. (The legacy single-world key `SAVE_KEY` = `minecraft_save_v7` is read only once, by the migration described under [Profiles & worlds](#profiles--worlds).)
